result.text: Dolwen Residential Care Home is a 32-bedroom facility that was built in the 1960s. It is struggling to meet the complex needs of citizens who require residential care. The purpose of the project is to provide premises that are fit for purpose, modern and accessible, and which have sufficient space for current and future provision. It will use digital technology and Artificial Intelligence. It will be well-located to provide care closer to home and meet the health and care needs of local people, including unmet needs, i.e. provision for the elderly who are mentally frail, and support service delivery within the building itself and in the local community. At present, the following issues need to be addressed at Dolwen home: - Small rooms which limit the service provider's ability to meet the needs of residents; for example, there are rooms that are suitable for hoists, but this is not the case throughout the facility. This restriction limits who can be provided with accommodation, depending on their needs. - None of the rooms are en-suite, and they do not offer sufficient living space or the facilities expected by modern standards. - The service provider is struggling to meet complex needs, which means it is not possible to provide accommodation for patients as they would like. A wide range of factors influences the proposal: - an expected increase in the older population of Denbighshire to 30.9% by 2040; including the fact that current facilities will not be suitable for the needs of residents; improving service provision; bringing services closer to the community; improving current provision for older people and the need to overcome limitations such as access, space and parking, and meeting Denbighshire's challenge and goal to be carbon neutral by 2030. This project, which is led by Denbighshire County Council (DCC) in collaboration with Community Housing, Denbighshire Voluntary Services Council and Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, is a project to review the potential development of Dolwen Residential Care Home. The project proposes an extension and modernisation work for Dolwen, including: - Residential capacity for the mentally frail elderly, i.e. developing a dementia wing. - Providing an extra care lite model in the older people's housing facility bordering Dolwen, in partnership with Community Housing. - A hub and spoke model of community support on an outreach and in-reach basis in conjunction with Community Housing and Denbighshire Voluntary Services Council. - Upgrading and modernising the current residential facility from 32 to 50 beds. This will include an extension and will enable the current accommodation to be redeveloped to ensure that it meets future complexity needs, e.g. a hoist in every room and en-suite facilities. - Improving current dementia support provisions in the community of Denbigh and the surrounding area. result.text: Procurement of an integrated chromatographic instrument and data management platform for an analytical research laboratory. Procurement, delivery, installation, configuration, integration, commissioning, training, documentation, warranty and support of a chromatography data system (CDS) as a central platform for instrument control, data acquisition, data processing, reporting, auditability and controlled management of chromatographic data. The CDS must support the integration of the analytical systems procured under lots 2 to 5 and provide functions for data integrity, user and role management as well as connection to institutional data management structures.; Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of a gas chromatography-mass spectrometry system with dual detector configuration consisting of a flame ionisation detector (FID) and single quadrupole mass spectrometer (MSD). The system is used for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of small molecules and metabolites in complex sample matrices and must support integration into the central chromatography data system (CDS).; Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of an ultra-high performance liquid chromatography system (UHPLC) with dual detection consisting of a PDA/DAD detector and a universal gradient-compatible detector for non-UV absorbing compounds. The system is used for the separation, detection and quantification of organic compounds in complex matrices and must support integration into the central chromatography data system (CDS).; Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of a single quadrupole LC-MS system with integrated liquid chromatography frontend. The system is used for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of small molecules, metabolites and impurities as well as for carrying out high-throughput screening workflows including flow injection analysis (FIA). Integration into the central chromatography data system (CDS) must be ensured.; Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of a semi-preparative HPLC system for the isolation, purification and recovery of organic compounds in the milligram to gram range. The system must support automated and traceable fraction collection, purification workflows as well as integration into the central chromatography data system (CDS).

parts.source: Beschaffung einer integrierten chromatographischen Instrumenten- und Datenmanagementplattform für analytisches Forschungslabor Beschaffung, Lieferung, Installation, Konfiguration, Integration, Inbetriebnahme, Schulung, Dokumentation, Gewährleistung und Support eines Chromatographiedatensystems (CDS) als zentrale Plattform für Gerätesteuerung, Datenerfassung, Datenverarbeitung, Berichterstellung, Auditierbarkeit und kontrollierte Verwaltung chromatographischer Daten. Das CDS muss die Integration der im Rahmen der Lose 2 bis 5 beschafften Analysensysteme unterstützen und Funktionen zur Datenintegrität, Benutzer- und Rollenverwaltung sowie zur Anbindung an institutionelle Datenmanagementstrukturen bereitstellen.; Beschaffung, Lieferung, Installation, Inbetriebnahme, Integration, Schulung, Dokumentation, Gewährleistung und Support eines Gaschromatographie-Massenspektrometrie-Systems mit Doppeldetektorkonfiguration bestehend aus Flammenionisationsdetektor (FID) und Single-Quadrupol-Massenspektrometer (MSD). Das System dient der qualitativen und quantitativen Analyse kleiner Moleküle und Metaboliten in komplexen Probenmatrizes und muss die Integration in das zentrale Chromatographiedatensystem (CDS) unterstützen.; Beschaffung, Lieferung, Installation, Inbetriebnahme, Integration, Schulung, Dokumentation, Gewährleistung und Support eines Ultra-High-Performance-Liquid-Chromatography-Systems (UHPLC) mit Doppeldetektion bestehend aus einem PDA-/DAD-Detektor und einem universellen gradientenkompatiblen Detektor für nicht UV-absorbierende Verbindungen. Das System dient der Trennung, Detektion und Quantifizierung organischer Verbindungen in komplexen Matrices und muss die Integration in das zentrale Chromatographiedatensystem (CDS) unterstützen.; Beschaffung, Lieferung, Installation, Inbetriebnahme, Integration, Schulung, Dokumentation, Gewährleistung und Support eines LC-MS-Single-Quadrupol-Systems mit integriertem Flüssigchromatographie-Frontend. Das System dient der qualitativen und quantitativen Analyse kleiner Moleküle, Metaboliten und Verunreinigungen sowie der Durchführung von Hochdurchsatz-Screening-Workflows einschließlich Flow Injection Analysis (FIA). Die Integration in das zentrale Chromatographiedatensystem (CDS) ist sicherzustellen.; Beschaffung, Lieferung, Installation, Inbetriebnahme, Integration, Schulung, Dokumentation, Gewährleistung und Support eines semipräparativen HPLC-Systems zur Isolierung, Aufreinigung und Rückgewinnung organischer Verbindungen im Milligramm- bis Grammbereich. Das System muss eine automatisierte und rückverfolgbare Fraktionssammlung, Aufreinigungsworkflows sowie die Integration in das zentrale Chromatographiedatensystem (CDS) unterstützen.

rejected.text: The term intends to enter into a contract for licences for the KI based tool Claude from the supplier Anthropic. Justification for the choice: The term needs an advanced, general KI-tool that can be used by employees across disciplines, including developers, designers and other roles. The aim is to support analysis, development and interaction assignments in line with Sikt's strategic targets for the use of artificial intelligence. After completed needs and market assessments, Visibility 檚 assessment is that Claude currently appears to be the best suitable solution for the purpose, particularly in light of: *support for secure and final user-controlled access to data and integrations based on open standards, **good interaction between different user groups, including close collaboration between developers and other professional environments, technical prerequisites for integration with Sikt's existing platform services and architecture. Visibility has assessed alternative systems in the market, including, among other things, Copilot, Gemini, ChatGPT and Cursor, but they are not currently assessed to cover the need to a sufficient degree, especially in terms of the combination of access management, integration options and use across roles. The market for KI tools is developing quickly. The choice of Claude is therefore based on an assessment of available systems at the time of the procurement and is not intended to establish any type of long-term standardisation or supplier binding. Procurement form: The term has examined the possibility of acquiring Claude through the existing framework agreement for software licenses, but has been confirmed that the product cannot be delivered through it. Direct procurements from Anthropic are thus the only available procurement route. Extent and value of the procurement: The procurement concerns licences for Claude, with a staged and needs managed employee disclosure. The estimated total contract value is NOK 3,500,000. The actual cost will depend on the number of users and actual use over time. Options: No options.

result.text: In the tender, SGAV will outsource the screening part of a large proportion of the field blocks and associated map themes that are to be 1. processed to the supplier. This screening must be carried out according to specific guidelines, cf. this Annex 1 (Situation description) and Annex 3 (Screening instructions). This concerns the screening of a limited number of field blocks of 60.000 – 120.000 annually, as SGAV itself handles certain field blocks, e.g. due to their high complexity, if there are proposals for changes to the field block, or if analyses show that there is a high probability that the field block or an associated map theme needs to be corrected. After the supplier's screening, SGAV will itself edit the field blocks and associated map themes where there is a need for editing. The supplier must, however, update certain attribute data for all the screened field blocks, as described in Annex 4 (Interface description). Assessment of the field blocks and the associated map themes by the supplier must be based in particular on orthophotos from the last three years, certain attribute data on the field blocks and the associated map themes, as well as the field drawings from the applicants.

Denne screening skal ske efter speci-fikke retningslinjer, jf. nærværende Bilag 1 (Situationsbeskrivelse) og Bilag 3 (Screeningsin-struks). Der er tale om screening af et afgrænset antal markblokke på 60.000 – 120.000 årligt, da SGAV selv håndterer visse markblokke f.eks. på grund af deres høje kompleksitet, hvis der er ændringsforslag til markblokken, eller hvis analyser viser, at der er stor sandsynlighed for, at markblokken eller et tilhørende korttema skal rettes. Efter leverandørens screening vil SGAV selv redigere de markblokke og tilhørende korttema-er, hvor der er behov for redigering. Vurdering af markblokkene og de tilhørende korttemaer hos leverandøren skal især ske på grundlag af ortofotos fra de seneste tre år, visse attributdata på markblokkene og de tilhøren-de korttemaer samt markindtegningerne fra ansøgerne.

rejected.text: Nygårdstunnelen in Bergen was opened in 1999 and is 864 metres long. The tunnel runs from the Puddefjord Bridge to Nygårdstangen, with exit ramps at O.J. Brochsgate. There are 2 lanes from the Puddefjord Bridge, whilst there are 1 lanes from O.J. Brochs gate. These meet in the tunnel so that there are 3 lanes at the exit and entrance at Nygårdstangen. The annual daily traffic is approx. 45,000. The tunnel shall be upgraded in accordance with the tunnel safety regulations and equipment in and outside the tunnel shall be replaced and replaced with new equipment that meets the current requirements. This includes, among other things: • New ventilation system. • New lighting installations with both new lights in the tunnel roof and continuous evacuation lights. • Extinguishing water shall be set up for the fire brigade. New system for handling emissions and tunnel washing water that fulfils emission requirements. • New signage with barriers, lane signal and variable signs. • Emergency stations with fire extinguishers and telephones. • Camera with coverage throughout the entire tunnel, which gives an alarm during events. • New technical building in the tunnel in the existing mountain room. • A new stop section shall be established at the technical building. • Demolition of existing air treatment plant.

result.text: Description Essex Record Office (ERO) is seeking to engage with the market to understand available solutions and supplier capabilities that can support the modernisation of its archive management, digital preservation and public access services. ERO is undertaking this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to inform future procurement activity and ensure that any proposed solutions align with the organisation's statutory responsibilities, service requirements and long-term digital preservation ambitions. ERO is looking to understand the market's ability to provide solutions that can deliver the following outcomes: • Replacement of the current in-house developed Archive Management System (SEAX), which underpins over 80% of ERO's operations and public-facing services, including income-generating online services. • The archive management system will need to: o facilitate viewing the catalogue on-site at Essex Record Office locations and online o provide free access to digital and digitised collections on-site at Essex Record Office locations o provide online access, outside of ERO locations, to digital and digitised collections via a subscription service o facilitate the creation of user accounts with role dependent security/access levels o provide a paywall to access certain collections o manage the personal data of users of the service, including taking payments from them • Support for statutory archive, records management and civil registration functions. • Secure, scalable and standards-compliant digital preservation capabilities to support the long-term preservation, integrity and accessibility of digital records. We require a solution for preserving digital records with retention periods of 100 years or more, as well as potentially shorter retention periods. The solution must be able to deal with a variety of file formats including proprietary software files and a range of sound and moving image files. • Progression towards National Digital Stewardship Alliance (NDSA) Level 4 digital preservation maturity. Specifically, we require: o For digital records storage: three copies in at least two geographic locations (storage will need to be in the UK or EU) o A means of controlling, auditing, and recording file permissions o A means of recording sufficient metadata about the files using an appropriate metadata standard e.g. METS (Metadata Encoding and Transmission Standard), PREMIS (PREservation Metadata: Implementation Strategies), BagIt (BagIt File Packaging Format) and/or Dublin Core o Periodic integrity checking and disaster simulation, and a means of regularly updating the results of these checks o A means of recording details of people and software that have accessed or taken preservation actions on files. • Improved management and discovery of digital assets through modern digital asset management capabilities. • Enhanced public access, search and discovery through modern online archive and catalogue services. • Improved customer journeys and increased public engagement. • Support for current income generating services and potential for enhanced income generation opportunities. • Integration capabilities with existing and future corporate platforms and digital services. • Modern, intuitive and user-friendly interfaces for both staff and public users. As a minimum, we will need: o The ability to allow members of the public to access suitable digital preservation files o A means of providing redacted access copies of the content where necessary o A means of recording when files have been accessed and by whom o A means of ensuring the content is protected from unauthorised changes and any loss • Scalable architecture capable of supporting current digital holdings of 88.8TB and significant future growth over the coming decades. • Strong governance, audit, compliance and security features to support statutory and regulatory requirements, including the Public Records Act, Freedom of Information legislation and Data Protection requirements. Background Archive Management System It is estimated that over 80% of the work of the ERO is currently managed through an in-house developed tool called SEAX. SEAX was created by Essex County Council as a bespoke system. It was created over 25 years ago in a now archaic programming language. Seax Explorer was written in VB (Visual Basic) and uses forms to create the different screens of its various modules (e.g. Catalogue Manager, Accession Manager, etc.). These forms have been written in a custom language based loosely around XML and are stored within the Seax Explorer database. The online element of the system is known internally as Seax PAM and to the public as Essex Archives Online. This includes our online catalogue and income-generating subscription service and income-generating single-image service. Seax PAM was written using .NET framework and C# and is currently using an old version of .NET framework. We are seeking a modern, sustainable and future-proofed solution for managing our requirements for accessioning, cataloguing, storage locations, document production, reader management and user access (at the ERO and online). The ERO has a staff of around 25 people. Up to 12 users are likely to require login access to the staff side of the AMS, including generic logins for Searchroom staff, document production staff, volunteers, etc. Digital Preservation As of July 2026, the ERO has 88.8TB of digital data. This figure is expected to grow at an estimated rate of 5TB per year. Within the 88.8TB of data, 3.3TB consists of born-digital records; the other 85.5TB being content the ERO has digitised from its manuscript, image, sound and video collections. This data is all currently stored on Microsoft Azure Cloud Storage. Most of the content is listed in basic form on a spreadsheet. Detailed metadata at file level is being added as resources allow.

Within the 88.8TB of data, 3.3TB consists of born-digital records; the other 85.5TB being content the ERO has digitised from its manuscript, image, sound and video collections. This data is all currently stored on Microsoft Azure Cloud Storage. Most of the content is listed in basic form on a spreadsheet. Detailed metadata at file level is being added as resources allow.

result.text: Further documentation about rights is kept in separate filing and on our archive management system (alongside information about our paper and analogue collections). The ERO has a dedicated ingest PC through which we process digital collections as they arrive. We are able to take images of disks using ISO Buster software, transfer files as they are or transfer them to a file format with greater longevity. Transfers can be made using Teracopy software and we can interrogate the files we receive using TNA’s Droid software. The main element of NDSA (National Digital Stewardship Alliance) Digital Preservation Level 1 we are not currently achieving is the requirement to have two complete copies of our digital content in separate locations. Our aim is to progress through the NDSA digital preservation levels to meet NDSA Level 4. The information gathered through this PME will help shape ERO's future procurement strategy, solution design and business case development. Lot 1: .

rejected.text: The Transport Phenomena (TP) programme supports fundamental research to understand, model, and control the transport of mass, momentum, energy, and species across multiple scales. Innovative TP research supports advances in artificial intelligence; manufacturing; biotechnology; microelectronics; energy generation, extraction, and utilisation; nuclear energy; quantum science and engineering; and other national priorities. TP projects involve experiments, theory, and/or computational modelling. They aim to improve understanding and to create novel analytical techniques. While projects focus on fundamental principles, they also have a clear vision of how research outcomes will benefit applications in engineering. TP supports research on the dynamics of single- and multiphase systems. Special interests include flow separation, transition to turbulence, drag reduction, cavitation, instabilities, and reactive flows. The programme encourages research on the connection between dynamics at the microscale and material and flow properties at the macroscale. Fluids of interest include liquids, gases, suspensions, emulsions, granular materials, active fluids, biological fluids, colloids, aerosols, bubbles and drops, and fluids with surfactants. TP supports research on physicochemical phenomena at the interfaces between fluids and between fluids and solids. These phenomena include adsorption and desorption of nanoparticles and surfactants; bulk and interfacial rheology; wetting and capillarity phenomena; electrokinetics; flow in porous media; and directed and self-assembly of particles. TP supports research on thermodynamics and thermal transport involving conduction, diffusion, convection, phase transition, and radiation. Research may be across scales, in complex structures and at interfaces, in microelectronic devices, and in biological systems. Projects involving phonon transport and quantum thermal phenomena are welcome. TP encourages proposals focused on combustion of gas, liquid and solid fuels. Combustion topics of interest include chemical kinetic modelling, turbulence-chemistry interactions, detonations, plasma assisted reacting flows, sustainable fuels, mechanisms for pollutant control, and in-situ diagnostic methods. The programme also supports research on wildland fire behaviour that aims to prevent wildfire spread, inhibit its growth, and/or predict and mitigate fires at the wildland-urban interface. Partnerships: To speed discovery and innovation, NSF partners with federal agencies, industry, international groups, and others. Current opportunities are at NSF ENG Partnerships.

result.text: By the present procurement procedure, the EIT KIC Urban Mobility S.L. hereby being referred to as “the EIT UM” or as “EIT UM” is aiming to procure the Workplace service (hereinafter referred to as the “Provider”), that would cover all aspects of the Endpoint user computers and key productivity tools are included within the scope of this service. The service required is composed of three main work packages: hardware provisioning (covering the supply and lifecycle of user devices), software licensing (managing procurement and compliance of key applications), and workplace support (providing user assistance and incident resolution). The aim of this RFP and the resulting agreement is to consolidate and enhance this model by integrating these key functions into a single, cohesive service. The selected vendor will work closely with EIT Urban Mobility’s internal Technology Department to deliver a coherent service fully aligned with the company’s strategic roadmap, while contributing added value through expertise, quality, and continuous improvement. EIT Urban Mobility currently has over 185 users (and over 210 including external collaborators). While most of the staff is based at the headquarters in Barcelona (Catalonia, Spain), EIT Urban Mobility also has employees in the following locations: • Munich (Germany) • Prague (Czech Republic) • Copenhagen (Denmark) • Helmond (The Netherlands) • Brussels (Belgium) Due to the nature of the company, with different locations across Europe, it is critical that a vast majority of the support functions are provided remotely via appropriate channels and tools. Additionally, all employees are authorised to work from home, therefore the IT support to be provided must also be easily accessible to all users who are teleworking. result.text: The Student Loans company (SLC) have an agreement for Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service expiring April 2028. In order to provision for a retender of the agreement SLC are undertaking pre-market engagement with regards to the provision of the following: • Requirement A: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service (2026-TR-0109a) • Requirement B: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management (VM) Service (2026-TR-0109b) • Requirement C: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) Service (2026-TR-0109c) • Requirement D: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Service (2026-TR-0109d) • Requirement E: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Retainer Service (2026-TR-0109e) • Requirement F: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture and Engineering Support Services (2026-TR-0109f) SLC is considering an approach to the market to give the suppliers an option to bid for one or ALL of the contractual requirements. Requirement A Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service The Supplier will provide a Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) capability operating on a hybrid customer/supplier model. MXDR Service The Supplier will provide: • 24x7x365 monitoring of SLC security telemetry. • L1 and L2 Security Operations Centre capability (SLC retain L3). • Incident identification, triage and investigation. • Security use-case monitoring and tuning. • Management of Microsoft Sentinel detections. • SOAR playbook execution and optimisation. • Escalation management. • Alert enrichment. • Threat hunting capability. • Malicious activity investigation. • Service governance and performance management. • Security reporting at operational, tactical and strategic levels. Security Engineering (Operational) The Supplier shall provide: • L3 Engineering support for Sentinel. • Analytics rule development and tuning. • SOAR playbook management. • Connector maintenance and health monitoring. • Logging optimisation. • Onboarding and validation of agreed log sources. • Detection engineering support. • Detection gap analysis and monitoring coverage reviews. • Security use case development and continuous improvement. • Monitoring health checks. • Monitoring and remediation of ingestion issues. • Security platform optimisation. • Proactive automation support and development. • Threat intelligence-led detection improvements. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) & Phishing The Supplier shall: • Monitoring, triage and investigation of DLP, phishing, business email compromise (BEC), malicious email, malicious attachment and malicious URL alerts. • Investigation of suspected data loss, data exfiltration and policy breach events. • Support for user reported phishing submissions. • Escalation and coordination of confirmed incidents in accordance with agreed response procedures. • Identification and analysis of phishing campaigns, attacker infrastructure, indicators of compromise and emerging attack trends. • Recommendations for improvements to DLP policies, email security controls, detections and response processes. • Monthly reporting, trend analysis and security improvement recommendations. Reporting The Supplier shall provide: • Weekly operational reports. • Monthly service reports. • Quarterly service reviews. • KPI and SLA reporting. • Security metrics and trend analysis. Requirement B Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management Service The Supplier shall provide Vulnerability Management services Monday to Friday, UK Core Hours (09:00-17:00). Vulnerability Management The Supplier shall: • Monitor vulnerability management queues. • Investigate vulnerability notifications. • Manage vulnerability triage. • Validate vulnerability findings. • Perform exploitability assessments. • Provide remediation recommendations. • Support exposure management activities. • Support CTEM activities. Stakeholder Engagement The Supplier shall: • Conduct monthly technical review meetings. • Support resolver teams. • Assist remediation planning. • Review remediation performance. • Provide vulnerability prioritisation guidance. Dashboarding & Reporting The Supplier shall: • Maintain executive dashboards. • Enhance Power BI reporting. • Produce technical reports. • Produce executive reports. • Produce PCI compliance reports. • Produce risk trending reports. Tooling The Supplier shall support: • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. • Rapid7. • SLC PCI ASV Scanning tooling. • Jira. • Power BI. Requirement C Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation Service The Supplier shall provide a Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) capability, currently using AttackIQ or similar. BAS Service The Supplier shall: • Operate and maintain the BAS platform. • Deploy and maintain BAS agents. • Configure integrations. • Execute scheduled simulations. • Execute customer-specific simulations. • Execute retests following remediation activities. Adversary Simulation Testing scenarios shall include: • Initial Access. • Execution. • Persistence. • Privilege Escalation. • Credential Access. • Lateral Movement. • Command and Control. • Exfiltration. • Malware. • Ransomware. • Advanced Persistent Threat activity. Security Validation The Supplier shall assess: • Security control effectiveness. • Security monitoring effectiveness. • Detection coverage. • Response capability. • Incident handling. • Use-case effectiveness. Reporting The Supplier shall produce: • Monthly BAS reports. • Executive summaries. • Technical findings. • Remediation recommendations. • Retest outcomes. Requirement D Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence Service The Supplier shall provide strategic, operational and tactical Cyber Threat Intelligence services.

parts.source: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης αποτελεί η «Λειτουργία, Συντήρηση, Υποστήριξη και Αναβάθμιση των πληροφοριακών συστημάτων “Εγγραφή στην Πρώτη Δημοτικού” και ηλεκτρονικών αιτήσεων εισαγωγής σε Πρότυπα Σχολεία, Δημόσια Ωνάσεια Σχολεία, Πρότυπα Εκκλησιαστικά Σχολεία και Πειραματικά Σχολεία». result.text: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to catalyze the translation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled, image-centered, multimodal CDS tools, developed as Software as a Medical Device, from training and testing of prototypes towards clinical applications that address unmet health challenges in precision medicine. These projects are expected to have high potential for demonstrable, positive impact on patient outcomes and/or healthcare processes.

rejected.text: Beschaffung einer Betriebsumgebung für das Geoportal-Hessen Das Hessische Landesamt für Bodenmanagement und Geoinformation ist eine Dienststelle des Landes Hessen und beherbergt unter anderem die zentrale Kompetenzstelle für Geoinformation. Diese ist gemäß § 3 Abs. 2 Nr. 2 der Verordnung zur Ausführung des Hessischen Vermessungs- und Geoinformationsgesetzes (HVGGAusfVO) für den Betrieb, die Administration und die Weiterentwicklung des Geoportals Hessen verantwortlich (§ 36 Abs. 2 HVGG). Das Geoportal Hessen (www.geoportal.hessen.de) ist der zentrale Zugangsknoten zur Geodateninfrastruktur Hessen (GDI-Hessen). Es dient als zentrale Plattform für Geodaten, Geodatendienste und die dazugehörigen Metadaten, die von der Landesverwaltung sowie von kommunalen Gebietskörperschaften bereitgestellt werden. Für den weiteren Betrieb sucht die zentrale Kompetenzstelle für Geoinformation einen IT-Dienstleister, der die notwendige Infrastruktur für den technischen Betrieb des Geoportals Hessen bereitstellt und betreibt. Das Frontend des Geoportals muss über das Internet zugänglich sein. Für die Wartung und Pflege der eingesetzten Softwarekomponenten ist ein gesicherter Fernzugriff über das NdB (Netz des Bundes) erforderlich. Ziel ist der Abschluss eines EVB-IT Vertrages. Alle Leistungen haben durch den Auftragnehmer in enger Abstimmung mit dem Auftraggeber zu erfolgen. Die Bereitstellung der Betriebsumgebung einschließlich aller Kommunikationsanforderungen entsprechend des Migrationsfahrplans Stufe 1 für das Geoportals Hessen hat bis 31.12.2026 zu erfolgen. Das Rechenzentrum des Auftragnehmers muss für den hochsicheren und hochverfügbaren Betrieb von Fachanwendungen ausgelegt sein und der Auftragnehmer muss über fundierte Erfahrungen im Betrieb komplexer IT-Fachverfahren verfügen. Die einzusetzende Software ist festgelegt, nicht Bestandteil der ausgeschriebenen Leistung und basiert ausschließlich auf Open Source Komponenten. Dazu gehören insbesondere: • Linux Betriebssystem (derzeit Debian), • Mapbender 2.8 (<3), • PostgreSQL mit PostGIS, • MapServer, • Django Framework, • MediaWiki. Die Software ist einsehbar unter: • https://github.com/GDI-HE/Mapbender2.8 und • https://github.com/GDI-HE/GeoPortal.rlp Die Software basiert auf den genannten Open Source Komponenten. Die GitHub-Links dienen der Konkretisierung der einzusetzenden Softwareversionen und stellen keine Produktvorgabe dar, sondern spezifizieren die funktionalen Anforderungen an die Betriebsumgebung. Weitere Details sind der Leistungsbeschreibung zu entnehmen.

result.text: Procurement of an operational environment for Geoportal Hessen. The Hessisches Landesamt für Bodenmanagement und Geoinformation is an agency of the Federal State of Hesse and houses, among other things, the central competence centre for geoinformation. In accordance with Section 3 paragraph 2 number 2 of the Ordinance for the Implementation of the Hessian Surveying and Geoinformation Act (HVGGAusfVO), this centre is responsible for the operation, administration and further development of Geoportal Hessen (Section 36 paragraph 2 HVGG). Geoportal Hessen (www.geoportal.hessen.de) is the central access node to the spatial data infrastructure of Hesse (GDI-Hessen). It serves as a central platform for spatial data, spatial data services and the associated metadata provided by the state administration and municipal local authorities. For its continued operation, the central competence centre for geoinformation is seeking an IT service provider to supply and operate the infrastructure necessary for the technical operation of Geoportal Hessen. The frontend of the geoportal must be accessible via the Internet. Secure remote access via the NdB (Federal Administration Network) is required for the maintenance and upkeep of the software components used. The objective is to conclude an EVB-IT contract. All services must be performed by the contractor in close coordination with the contracting authority. The provision of the operational environment, including all communication requirements in accordance with the migration roadmap stage 1 for Geoportal Hessen, must take place by 31.12.2026. The contractor's data centre must be designed for the highly secure and highly available operation of specialist applications, and the contractor must have sound experience in operating complex specialist IT procedures. The software to be used is fixed, does not form part of the tendered services and is based exclusively on open-source components. These include in particular: • Linux operating system (currently Debian), • Mapbender 2.8 (<3), • PostgreSQL with PostGIS, • MapServer, • Django framework, • MediaWiki. The software can be viewed at: • https://github.com/GDI-HE/Mapbender2.8 and • https://github.com/GDI-HE/GeoPortal.rlp The software is based on the aforementioned open-source components. The GitHub links serve to specify the software versions to be used and do not constitute a product specification, but rather specify the functional requirements for the operational environment. Further details can be found in the specification of services.

Die Bereitstellung der Betriebsumgebung einschließlich aller Kommunikationsanforderungen entsprechend des Migrationsfahrplans Stufe 1 für das Geoportals Hessen hat bis 31.12.2026 zu erfolgen. Das Rechenzentrum des Auftragnehmers muss für den hochsicheren und hochverfügbaren Betrieb von Fachanwendungen ausgelegt sein und der Auftragnehmer muss über fundierte Erfahrungen im Betrieb komplexer IT-Fachverfahren verfügen. Die einzusetzende Software ist festgelegt, nicht Bestandteil der ausgeschriebenen Leistung und basiert ausschließlich auf Open Source Komponenten. Dazu gehören insbesondere: • Linux Betriebssystem (derzeit Debian), • Mapbender 2.8 (<3), • PostgreSQL mit PostGIS, • MapServer, • Django Framework, • MediaWiki. Die Software ist einsehbar unter: • https://github.com/GDI-HE/Mapbender2.8 und • https://github.com/GDI-HE/GeoPortal.rlp Die Software basiert auf den genannten Open Source Komponenten. Die GitHub-Links dienen der Konkretisierung der einzusetzenden Softwareversionen und stellen keine Produktvorgabe dar, sondern spezifizieren die funktionalen Anforderungen an die Betriebsumgebung. Weitere Details sind der Leistungsbeschreibung zu entnehmen.

This is a fixed-price contract and must include all costs associated with delivery, including project management, user research, service design, WordPress development, accessibility testing, quality assurance, knowledge transfer, stakeholder engagement, travel, subsistence, overheads, licences and any other expenses. Suppliers will be required to submit a breakdown of costs by deliverable and milestone as part of their tender response About the work Why the work is being done Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) is seeking to improve the accessibility, usability and effectiveness of its website to better support health and social care professionals, partner organisations, citizens and communities across Scotland. User testing and stakeholder feedback have identified challenges relating to navigation, information architecture, content discovery and overall user experience. These issues can make it difficult for users to find and access important information, resources, tools, standards, frameworks and publications. HIS wishes to adopt a people-led, user-centred approach to improve access to information and digital services while building internal capability to sustainably manage and develop the website in the future. The project will focus initially on two directorates, creating reusable design patterns, templates and approaches that can subsequently be applied across the wider HIS web estate. The successful supplier will undertake discovery, user research, service design, accessibility improvement, WordPress development, implementation and knowledge transfer activities. The contract is expected to commence in November 2026 and all contracted deliverables must be completed by 30 June 2027. Problem to be solved Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) has identified challenges with the usability, accessibility and effectiveness of its website. User testing and stakeholder feedback have highlighted difficulties with navigation, information architecture, content discovery and overall user experience. These issues make it harder for users to find and access important information, resources, standards, tools, frameworks and publications, reducing engagement and limiting the impact of nationally important content. HIS is seeking a supplier to help create a more user-centred, accessible and sustainable digital service. Working within the existing WordPress platform, the supplier should focus on understanding user needs and applying a people-led design approach to improve how users find, access and interact with content. The initial scope focuses on two HIS directorates and aims to create reusable design patterns, templates, components and approaches that can later be adopted across the wider HIS web estate. The successful supplier will also be expected to build internal capability through knowledge transfer, coaching and guidance. The outcomes sought are: • Improved accessibility, usability and user experience. • Improved navigation and information architecture. • Improved discoverability and use of HIS resources and digital content. • Reusable website templates, components and design approaches. • Increased adoption and use of HIS programmes and resources. • Greater internal capability through knowledge transfer and coaching. • Sustainable content management, governance and maintenance arrangements. Challenges include working within an existing WordPress environment, balancing multiple stakeholder needs, delivering improvements within a fixed budget, and ensuring outputs developed for the initial scope can be scaled across the wider HIS website. Who the users are and what they need to do As a health and social care professional, I need to quickly find guidance, standards, frameworks, publications, tools and resources so that I can use Healthcare Improvement Scotland information in my work. As a citizen or community member, I need to access information about Healthcare Improvement Scotland and its work so that I can understand and engage with health and care improvement activities. As a website user, I need to find information quickly and easily so that I can access the resources, publications and content relevant to my needs.

result.text: Market consultation: Construction management software for public administration in state building construction and federal building construction 1. Aim of the market consultation: As part of the modernisation of our construction-related IT infrastructure, we are conducting a market consultation. The aim is to identify potential solutions that offer user-friendly and secure support for state- and federal-specific requirements for kameralistic and construction-related IT-supported processing of the state and federal construction programme for the Federal State of Saxony-Anhalt. The construction management software must ensure the uniform, efficient processing of all necessary procedures for this and map a complete adoption of the business processes corresponding to the state standard for Saxony-Anhalt in state and federal construction, including interfaces and specific reporting. The solution approaches must be seamlessly integrable into the existing IT landscape, including cooperation with the IT service provider Dataport AöR and its requirements, as well as meeting the requirements for data protection and IT security in the KRITIS sector. This market consultation serves exclusively to gather information and runs until 17.03.2026. 2. Target group: The market consultation is aimed at suppliers who have experience in creating state-specific construction management software for state building construction and federal building construction within the framework of administrative assistance (Organleihe), including the applicable regulations and standards of the state and the federal government, as well as their seamless integration into existing hybrid and complex IT system landscapes in the KRITIS environment.

Ziel der Markterkundung: Im Rahmen der Modernisierung unserer baufachlichen IT-Infrastruktur führen wir eine Markterkundung durch. Ziel ist es, mögliche Lösungen zu identifizieren, die eine benutzerfreundliche und sichere Begleitung der landes- und bundesspezifischen Anforderungen an die kameralistische und baufachliche IT-gestützte Bearbeitung des Landes- und Bundesbauprogrammes für das Land Sachsen-Anhalt bieten. Die Baumanagementsoftware soll die einheitliche, effiziente Bearbeitung aller dafür notwendigen Vorgänge sicherstellen und eine vollständige Übernahme der nach der Landesnorm für Sachsen-Anhalt im Landes- und Bundesbau entsprechenden Geschäftsprozesse inkl. Schnittstellen, das spezifischen Berichtswesen abbilden. Die Lösungsansätze müssen nahtlos in die bestehende IT-Landschaft inkl. der Zusammenarbeit mit dem IT-Dienstleister Dataport AöR und dessen Anforderungen integrierbar sein, sowie den Anforderungen an Datenschutz und IT-Sicherheit im KRITIS-Sektor entsprechen. Diese Markterkundung dient ausschließlich der Informationsgewinnung und läuft bis zum 17.03.2026. 2. Zielgruppe: Die Markterkundung richtet sich an Anbieter, die Erfahrungen in der Erstellung einer landesspezifischen Baumanagementsoftware für den Staatlichen Landesbau und Bun-desbau im Rahmen der Organleihe inkl. der gelten Regularien und Normen des Landes und des Bundes sowie deren nahtlose Integration in bestehende hybride und komplexe IT-Systemlandschaften im KRITIS-Umfeld haben.

result.text: Südwestrundfunk (SWR), as a public service broadcaster of the ARD, is strictly dependent on a functioning IT infrastructure to fulfil its tasks. In the age of digital communication, central elements are necessary for efficient process control in order to be able to plan, execute, and implement processes digitally, both internally and across the entire ARD. Different software solutions for network management are currently in use at Südwestrundfunk and the eligible state broadcasting corporations. The network management tool CheckMK is already in use across the board at a large number of the eligible entities and is deeply integrated into the system landscape. As part of the ARD structural reform, a holistic solution is to be established across the entire ARD. For this purpose, services for the Checkmk product are to be procured for Südwestrundfunk and other eligible state broadcasting corporations. Furthermore, the eligible entities require further services such as consulting and support in the area of network management and for the CheckMK product. Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Delivery services Services of the Checkmk product incl. support for a limited period. - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Advance payment guarantee Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 17 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 1) The acceptance quantities for Lot 1 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 5.6 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Number of services in units for Checkmk incl. support: Minimum acceptance quantity: 1.000.000 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 1.400.000 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1.800.000 units Acceptance quantities Checkmk Synthetic Monitoring: Minimum acceptance quantity: 10 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 200 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 500 units Acceptance quantities virtual appliances: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1 units per licence scale up to 600.000 services Lot 2: - result.text: NRW.BANK is the largest state promotional bank in Germany. It employs approximately 1650 members of staff and, with a total assets of approximately 162 billion euros, ranks 11 among all banks in Germany. It consists of 19 divisions with a total of 250 organisational units and 232 managers, of which 5 are dual leadership roles. Since 2022, a cultural change initiative has been underway within the bank, the results of which include the design of a mission statement with strong requirement criteria for collaboration, initiative, efficiency and personal responsibility. Culture pilots support implementation in the 19 divisions of the bank. In parallel with this, alongside the traditional run organisation for ongoing business processes, an agile delivery organisation has been and is currently being established in which larger change projects are bundled into agile-working teams. The organisational structure has not been changed in this context, i.e. the members of staff seconded wholly or partly to the agile delivery organisation also remain attached to managers in the existing organisational structure. The scope of the contract includes the preparation, execution and follow-up of an annual staff survey. The contractor shall conduct the surveys using an online survey instrument. The first survey shall be conducted in September 2026. The notification of all managers regarding the survey results for their areas of responsibility must have taken place by November 2026 at the latest. The workshops for processing the survey results shall follow immediately after the first survey and take place on demand. Following the first survey, the cycle for subsequent surveys shall be determined: this can be 12, 18 or 24 months. Further details can be found in the specification of requirements (Annex 1) or the framework agreement.

parts.source: Die NRW.BANK ist das größte Landesförderinstitut in Deutschland. Sie beschäftigt ca. 1650 Mitarbeitende und liegt mit einer Bilanzsumme von ca. 162 Milliarden Euro auf Platz 11 aller Banken in Deutschland. Sie besteht aus 19 Bereichen mit insgesamt 250 Organisationseinheiten und 232 Führungskräften, davon 5 Doppelspitzen. Seit dem Jahr 2022 findet in der Bank eine Kulturwandelinitiative statt, die im Ergebnis u.a. ein Leitbild entworfen hat mit starken Anforderungskriterien zu Zusammenarbeit, Initiative, Effizienz und Eigenverantwortlichkeit. Kulturlotsen unterstützen die Umsetzung in den 19 Bereichen der Bank. Parallel hierzu wurde und wird zurzeit neben der klassischen Run-Organisation für die laufenden Geschäftsprozesse eine agile Lieferorganisation aufgebaut in der größere Veränderungsvorhaben in agil arbeitenden Teams gebündelt werden. Die Aufbauorganisation wurde in diesem Zusammenhang nicht verändert, d.h. auch die ganz oder teilweise in die agile Lieferorganisation entsandten Mitarbeitenden sind weiterhin an Führungskräfte der bestehenden Aufbauorganisation angebunden. Der Umfang des Auftrags beinhaltet die Vorbereitung, Durchführung und Nachbereitung einer jährlichen Befragung der Mitarbeitenden. Die Befragungen führt die Auftragnehmerin unter Verwendung eines Online-Befragungsinstruments durch. Die erste Befragung wird im September 2026 durchgeführt. Die Information aller Führungskräfte über die Befragungsergebnisse ihrer Zuständigkeitsbereiche soll spätestens im November 2026 erfolgt sein. Die Workshops zur Bearbeitung der Befragungsergebnisse schließen unmittelbar an die erste Befragung an und erfolgen auf Abruf. Nach der ersten Befragung wird der Turnus für die Folgebefragungen festgelegt: Dieser kann 12, 18 oder 24 Monate betragen. Nähere Details sind der Leistungsbeschreibung (Anlage 1) bzw. der Rahmenvereinbarung zu entnehmen.

rejected.text: The subject of the procurement is nurse call, fall detection, and mobility monitoring systems for use by Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala. Nurse call systems are used in the social welfare, healthcare, and rescue services sector in hospitals, senior centres, sheltered housing facilities, enhanced sheltered housing units, health centre ward departments, rehabilitation units, and other operating environments requiring 24-hour care and monitoring. In addition, the systems are utilised in home care support services and special units where clients' need for help can be sudden and require a response. Nurse call systems are a central part of daily care work and client and patient safety. They ensure that requests for help are transmitted without delay to the correct staff and that nursing staff are able to prioritize their tasks according to the urgency of the situation. At the same time, they support staff occupational safety in threat and hazardous situations, for example, and enable operational monitoring, reporting, and development. The importance of nurse call systems is particularly emphasized in situations where clients' functional capacity has deteriorated, memory disorders are common, or the need for care is continuous. In such cases, the system's operational reliability, ease of use, and integration with other systems are not merely technical features, but factors directly affecting the quality and safety of care. The objective of the procurement is to ensure that the solutions in use meet current and future needs. This requires the systems to be scalable, compatible with other technologies, and capable of adapting to various care environments without complicating the use of the systems. At the same time, it is ensured that the solutions to be procured fulfil obligations concerning data protection, information security, and regulatory requirements. As a whole, nurse call systems are a critical part of the functionality of the service system, and their procurement must be implemented in a way that long-term supports the quality, safety, and cost-efficiency of services. The objective of the framework agreement procurement is to find a maximum of five suppliers capable of delivering a nurse call system to the sector's sites that can handle traditional nurse calls (client/patient can call a nurse to the room) and additionally utilise new technology enabling the system to alert a nurse to the client's/patient's location proactively regarding risk situations (e.g. getting out of bed, falling). The new technology aims to improve client/patient safety within the limits defined by law. A nurse call system is required in all new and renovated hospitals, senior centres, etc. In addition, the social welfare, healthcare, and rescue services sector has several sites where a previously procured but outdated nurse call system no longer has maintenance and support offered by the supplier. These outdated systems must be replaced with new ones. The solutions forming the subject of the procurement are primarily procured as a comprehensive service provided by the suppliers selected for the framework agreement. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tender.

In such cases, the system's operational reliability, ease of use, and integration with other systems are not merely technical features, but factors that directly affect the quality and safety of care. The objective of the procurement is to ensure that the solutions in use meet current and future needs. This requires the systems to be scalable, compatible with other technologies, and capable of adapting to various care environments without complicating the use of the systems. At the same time, it is ensured that the solutions to be procured fulfil obligations regarding data protection, information security, and official requirements. Overall, nurse call systems are a critical part of the functionality of the service system, and their procurement must be carried out in a way that long-term supports the quality, safety, and cost-efficiency of services. The aim of the tendering procedure for the framework arrangement is to find up to five suppliers capable of delivering a nurse call system to the sector's sites that can handle traditional nurse calls (a client/patient can call a nurse to the room) and additionally utilise new technology that allows the system to proactively alert a nurse to the client's/patient's location in connection with risk situations (e.g., getting out of a bed, falling). The new technology aims to improve client/patient safety within the limits defined by law. A nurse call system is required in all new and renovated hospitals, senior centres, etc. In addition, the social, health, and rescue sector has several sites where a nurse call system was procured in the past but has become obsolete, and for which the supplier no longer provides maintenance and support. These obsolete systems must be replaced with new ones. The solutions that are the subject of the procurement will primarily be acquired as a comprehensive service provided by the suppliers selected for the framework arrangement. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tenders.

parts.source: Hankinnan kohteena on Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimialan käyttöön tulevat hoitajakutsu-, kaatumisentunnistus- sekä liikkumisen seurantajärjestelmät. Hoitajakutsujärjestelmiä käytetään sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimialalla sairaaloissa, seniorikeskuksissa, palvelutaloissa, tehostetun palveluasumisen yksiköissä, terveysasemien vuodeosastoilla, kuntoutusyksiköissä sekä muissa ympärivuorokautista hoitoa ja valvontaa edellyttävissä toimintaympäristöissä. Lisäksi järjestelmiä hyödynnetään kotihoidon tukipalveluissa ja erityisyksiköissä, joissa asiakkaiden avuntarve voi olla äkillistä ja reagointia edellyttävää. Hoitajakutsujärjestelmät ovat keskeinen osa päivittäistä hoiva, - ja hoitotyötä ja asiakas- sekä potilasturvallisuutta. Niiden avulla varmistetaan, että avunpyynnöt välittyvät viiveettä oikealle henkilöstölle ja että hoitohenkilökunta pystyy priorisoimaan tehtävänsä tilanteen kiireellisyyden mukaan. Samalla ne tukevat henkilöstön työturvallisuutta esimerkiksi uhka- ja vaaratilanteissa sekä mahdollistavat toiminnan seurannan, raportoinnin ja kehittämisen. Hoitajakutsujärjestelmien merkitys korostuu erityisesti tilanteissa, joissa asiakkaiden toimintakyky on heikentynyt, muistisairaudet ovat yleisiä tai hoidon tarve on jatkuvaa. Tällöin järjestelmän toimintavarmuus, helppokäyttöisyys ja integraatio muihin järjestelmiin eivät ole pelkästään teknisiä ominaisuuksia, vaan suoraan hoidon laatuun ja turvallisuuteen vaikuttavia tekijöitä. Hankinnan tavoitteena on varmistaa, että käytössä olevat ratkaisut vastaavat nykyisiä ja tulevia tarpeita. Tämä edellyttää järjestelmiltä skaalautuvuutta, yhteensopivuutta muiden teknologioiden kanssa sekä kykyä mukautua erilaisiin hoitoympäristöihin ilman, että järjestelmien käyttö monimutkaistuu. Samalla varmistetaan, että hankittavat ratkaisut täyttävät tietosuojaa, tietoturvaa ja viranomaisvaatimuksia koskevat velvoitteet. Kokonaisuutena hoitajakutsujärjestelmät ovat kriittinen osa palvelujärjestelmän toimivuutta, ja niiden hankinta tulee toteuttaa siten, että se tukee pitkäjänteisesti palveluiden laatua, turvallisuutta ja kustannustehokkuutta. Puitejärjestelyn kilpailutuksessa on tavoitteena löytää enintään viisi toimittajaa, jotka kykenevät toimittamaan toimialan kohteisiin hoitajakutsujärjestelmän, jolla voidaan hoitaa perinteinen hoitajakutsu (asiakas/potilas voi kutsua hoitajan huoneeseen) ja lisäksi hyödyntää uutta teknologiaa, jonka avulla järjestelmä voi hälyttää hoitajan asiakkaan/potilaan luokse ennakoivasti riskitilanteisiin liittyen (esim. sängyltä nouseminen, kaatuminen). Uuden teknologian avulla pyritään parantamaan asiakas/potilasturvallisuutta lain määrittämissä rajoissa. Hoitajakutsujärjestelmä tarvitaan kaikkiin uusiin ja saneerattaviin sairaaloihin, seniorikeskuksiin jne. Lisäksi sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimialalla on useita kohteita, joissa aikoinaan hankittu, mutta vanhentunut hoitajakutsujärjestelmä, jolle toimittaja ei enää tarjoa ylläpitoa ja tukea. Nämä vanhentuneet järjestelmät pitää korvata uusilla. Hankinnan kohteena olevat ratkaisut hankintaan pääasiassa puitejärjestelyyn valittujen toimittajien tarjoamana kokonaispalveluna. Tarkemmin hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tämän tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.

result.text: UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. Lot 1: . University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, "UCLH", is one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom and provides first-class acute and specialist services. UCLH comprises of the following hospitals: University College Hospital, Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing, MacMillan Cancer Centre, University College Hospital Grafton Way Building, University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street, Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals, National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine, and the Institute of Sport, Exercise and Health. UCLH delivers world class cancer care to patients from across the country. Cancer at UCLH spans across multiple sites and departments within the Trust and has included the opening of the Grafton Way Building one of two national Proton Beam Therapy services in December 2021. UCLH is a lead provider within the North Central London Cancer Alliance, as well as providing tertiary services for wider patient populations in specialist services, such as sarcoma for patients from across South East England. In early 2020, UCLH was selected by NHS England as the preferred tertiary cancer provider to take over management of the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre. This transition is subject to a due diligence process during which UCLH are providing transitional support to the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre team, building upon a number of years of collaborative working between the two services. Our Radiotherapy department offers cutting edge and specialised therapy to adult and paediatric patients treating over 2400 new patients a year. UCLH Radiotherapy is a national leader in complex/highly technical radiotherapy in: • Brain and was recently designated a Tessa Jowell Brain Cancer Centre of Excellence • Paediatrics, with the largest paediatric radiotherapy unit in the UK • Sarcomas - one of Europe’s largest service • Head and Neck – (ENT) third largest in the UK • Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (SABR) • Haematological including total body radiation • Brachytherapy • Molecular Radiotherapy - National Referral centre (Paediatric, TYA and adult). The department works closely with a number of specialist hospitals to support cancer pathways which span multiple centres including Great Ormond Street, St. Mary's, Oxford, Southampton and the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital. The UCH radiotherapy department contains six bunkers with four Varian TrueBeams and one Varian Halcyon. There is a large difference between the national and UCLH complexity profile, 92% of the UCH workload is classed as complex and approximately 8% of the workload is paediatric. The radiotherapy service is delivered by a team of staff including clinical oncologists, radiotherapy physics and engineers, therapeutic radiographers, healthcare play specialists, admin and clerical staff and dedicated nurses. UCLH is also one of two national Proton Beam Therapy centres, providing services to patients from the south of the UK. The departments run an integrated workforce model, with physicists, dosimetrists and radiographers rotating across Radiotherapy and PBT. In total there are around 300 WT across both services. UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. This could include but is not limited to: • Delivering Cancer Waiting Time Access standards. • Scheduling of patients. • Machine downtime. • Patient pathway and organisation of workflow. • Radiotherapy physics pathways. • Process for commissioning of new linacs. • Use of automation and AI. Expression of Interest The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to engage with potential partners to gather information and insights from the market to aid the development of the requirements and scope of opportunities for efficiencies to inform the procurement of a transformation partner. Suppliers are requested to provide expressions of interest, including responses to the below questions by e-mail to steviejay.cavanagh@nhs.net by 15:00 on 26th September 2025. 1. What innovative or new ways of working are you currently seeing in the market that may benefit the NHS, and more specifically UCLH, including those that have been included in procurements over the past 12 months? 2. Please describe how you think this contract should be best structured to deliver an efficient Radiotherapy service? 3. Is there anything you think that the Trust should consider before going out to market for these services? 4. What would be your expectations from a partnership with an NHS organisation? This notice does not constitute a formal call for competition. result.text: Provision must be undertaken for a turnkey solution that integrates specialised computing infrastructure, an AI/ML software platform, implementation and deployment services, development of Generative Artificial Intelligence use cases, training, ecosystem dynamisation, communication and outreach, specialised consultancy support, and maintenance and administration of the platform. The solution must enable PROCESA to have an operational ecosystem, governed locally and accessible to different user profiles, that facilitates the use of computing resources, storage, models, APIs, workspaces and associated services, ensuring the availability, security, traceability and continuity of the services provided. The object of the contract is not limited to the isolated provision of technological infrastructure, nor to the independent execution of training or dynamisation actions, but comprises the creation of a stable system for the adoption of Artificial Intelligence that makes it possible to reduce technical barriers to access, strengthen the technological autonomy of the territory, develop in-house capabilities and generate economic, social and organisational impact in a sustainable manner in the Autonomous City of Ceuta.

parts.source: Se ha de acometer la provisión de una solución llave en mano que integre infraestructura de computación especializada, plataforma software IA/ML, servicios de implantación y despliegue, desarrollo de casos de uso de Inteligencia Artificial Generativa, formación, dinamización del ecosistema, comunicación y divulgación, acompañamiento consultivo especializado y mantenimiento y administración de la plataforma. La solución deberá permitir a PROCESA disponer de un ecosistema operativo, gobernado localmente y accesible a distintos perfiles de usuario, que facilite el uso de recursos de cómputo, almacenamiento, modelos, APIs, entornos de trabajo y servicios asociados, asegurando la disponibilidad, seguridad, trazabilidad y continuidad de los servicios prestados. El objeto del contrato no se limita a la provisión aislada de infraestructura tecnológica, ni a la ejecución independiente de acciones formativas o de dinamización, sino que comprende la creación de un sistema estable de adopción de la Inteligencia Artificial que permita reducir barreras técnicas de acceso, fortalecer la autonomía tecnológica del territorio, desarrollar capacidades propias y generar impacto económico, social y organizativo de forma sostenible en la Ciudad Autónoma de Ceuta.

result.text: An observation instrument for children's linguistic and mathematical development is to be developed, pilot tested, validated and tested for reliability, derived from the Brandenburg curriculum. The items for assessing children's competences at the end of the Kita period (3 third of the final Kita year) are designed as "Individual learning status analysis at the transition from Kita to school (ILeA 0)" and configured to be compatible with the existing observation instrument for the "Individual learning status analysis in the first 6 weeks after starting school (ILeA plus)". The aim is an integrated, structurally harmonised observation system that records linguistic and mathematical development in a comparable and compatible structure. Lot LOT-0001: Development, pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of an observation instrument for linguistic and mathematical development. The contracting authority expects a standardised, scientifically sound, streamlined and practice-oriented observation instrument. A uniform conceptual approach is of central importance to the contracting authority in order to keep the need for qualification in practice to a low level and to simplify use by educational professionals with the uniform structure of ILeA 0. The service is divided into four work packages: Work package 1 (development of the linguistic aspects of the observation instrument), work package 2 (development of the mathematical aspects of the observation instrument), work package 3 (creation of a guidance document for the observation instrument), work package 4 (pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of the developed observation instrument). Further details can be found in Appendix 12 (specification of services).

parts.source: Es soll ein Beobachtungsinstrument der sprachlichen und mathematischen Entwicklung von Kindern entwickelt, pilotiert, validiert und auf Reliabilität geprüft werden, das sich aus dem Bildungsplan Brandenburg ableitet. Die Items zur Kompetenzerfassung von Kindern am Ende der Kita-Zeit (3. Drittel des letzten Kita-Jahres) werden als "Individuelle Lernstandsanalyse am Übergang Kita-Schule (ILeA 0)" konzipiert und an das bereits vorhandene Beobachtungsinstrument für die "Individuelle Lernstandsanalyse in den ersten 6 Wochen nach dem Schuleintritt (ILeA plus)" anschlussfähig ausgestaltet. Ziel ist ein integriertes, strukturell harmonisiertes Beobachtungssystem, das die sprachliche und mathematische Entwicklung in vergleichbarer und anschlussfähiger Struktur erfasst. Lot LOT-0001: Entwicklung, Pilotierung, Validierung und Reliabilitätsprüfung eines Beobachtungsinstruments der sprachlichen und mathematischen Entwicklung. Der Auftraggeber erwartet ein standardisiertes, wissenschaftlich fundiertes, schlankes und praxisorientiertes Beobachtungsinstrument. Für den Auftraggeber ist ein einheitlicher konzeptioneller Ansatz von zentraler Bedeutung, um den Qualifizierungsbedarf in der Praxis gering zu halten sowie die Nutzung durch die pädagogischen Fachkräfte mit der einheitlichen Struktur von ILeA 0 zu vereinfachen. Die Leistung ist aufgeteilt in vier Arbeitspakete: Arbeitspaket 1 (Entwicklung der sprachlichen Aspekte des Beobachtungsinstruments), Arbeitspaket 2 (Entwicklung der mathematischen Aspekte des Beobachtungsinstrumentes), Arbeitspaket 3 (Erstellen einer Handreichung zum Beobachtungsinstrument), Arbeitspaket 4 (Pilotierung, Validierung und Reliabilitätsprüfung des entwickelten Beobachtungsinstruments). Näheres ist der Anlage 12 (Leistungsbeschreibung) zu entnehmen.

result.text: HESA (part of Jisc) are seeking a supplier to support the annual coding of occupational information. Following its merger with the Higher Education Statistics Agency, Jisc has retained 'HESA' as a brand name, and Jisc's functions, activities and role as the DDB are undertaken by a dedicated directorate within Jisc, operating under the HESA brand. References to HESA within the Specification do not mean any legal entity. This will include Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) and Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) codes from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), along with some additional information to supplement this. The supply of this data will support our role as the designated data body for the HE sector, ensuring high quality, consistent classification of employer data. As survey responses are received, HESA/Jisc will securely make available to the supplier, in batches, an overnight file of the employer, course and role information to enable the supplier to complete the required SIC and SOC coding and return it to HESA/Jisc using an encrypted secure bulk data sending system. In addition to the purposes set out below, the coding will be used by Jisc to update and feed into the Graduate Outcomes provider dashboards so that Providers have visibility of the progress and outcomes of the coding. HESA/Jisc will run the Graduate Outcomes survey, working with third-party suppliers to manage the call centre system for contact management and to provide an online survey. It will be necessary for the supplier to join review calls with HESA/Jisc and HESA/Jisc's third-party suppliers to feedback any improvements required to the job role and employer data to improve the accuracy of coding. Lot LOT-0000: .

rejected.text: NHS Scotland intends to procure a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme to support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes. The programme will deliver a structured, evidence-based lifestyle intervention through a digital platform, including access to health coaching, peer support, and tools to support behaviour change and self-management. The procurement is expected to be undertaken via a Restricted Procedure, with a single supplier appointed to a national framework. Lot 1: . This Prior Information Notice (PIN) relates to NHS Scotland’s intention to tender for a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme. The programme will identify individuals at risk of Type 2 Diabetes based on clinical indicators (including HbA1c and fasting plasma glucose levels) or a previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes. It will provide a tailored, nine-month, evidence-based lifestyle intervention aimed at reducing the risk of progression to Type 2 Diabetes. The digital service will support Service Users via an application-based platform, providing access to trained health coaches, online peer support communities, and functionality to set, track, and monitor personalised health goals. The successful bidder will be required to deliver the programme in a way that is inclusive and accessible to Service Users from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. This will including ensuring the service is culturally sensitive to local populations and flexible enough to meet the needs of users with diverse requirements, including appropriate language support. Participants will be able to access the programme through multiple referral routes, including Primary Care (e.g. GP referral) and self-referral pathways. Current funding has been allocated to support up to 15,000 users over a three-year period. The proposed framework will operate as a single-supplier arrangement and will also include provision for the delivery of a Hypertension Pathway for approximately 500 users per annum. Eligibility for the hypertension pathway will be based on a confirmed diagnosis of primary hypertension alongside a BMI ≥25 (or BMI ≥23 for minority ethnic groups). Please Note: During the term of the Framework Agreement, NHS Scotland reserves the right, should funding become available, to increase the volume of service users (current estimate of 15000 over the initial 3-years of the Framework Agreement term) who may access the Programme. For example, additional purchases may be made which exceed the level of funding currently secured as a result of clinical and service outcomes and benefits which support wider adoption of the Programme. The Authority also reserves the right to expand the scope of the service to include additional cohorts, pathways, or clinical indicators (for example, the inclusion of further at-risk populations identified through screening), which may increase overall demand under the Framework. The procurement is expected to be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising two stages: Stage 1 Selection Stage (SPD Assessment): Suppliers will be required to complete and submit a Single Procurement Document (SPD). This stage will assess bidders’ suitability to proceed and will include a combination of pass/fail criteria (e.g. mandatory and discretionary exclusion grounds, economic and financial standing) and scored evaluation. As part of the SPD, the Authority will assess technical and professional ability, including responses to scored questions and requests for relevant examples of previous experience. These responses will be weighted and scored to enable the Authority to evaluate capability and rank suppliers. A shortlist of the highest-ranking bidders will be invited to progress to Stage 2. Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender (ITT): Only suppliers shortlisted at Stage 1 will be invited to submit a full tender. Bidders will be required to respond to a Statement of Requirements (SoR), setting out how they will deliver the contract, including proposed methodology, service delivery model, and pricing. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the published award criteria, based on quality and price, to determine the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT). Stage 1 is expected to commence mid to late August 2026, with Stage 2 anticipated to commence in early October 2026.. This project is derived from the Accelerated National Innovation Adoption (ANIA) Pathway. This is an initiative focused on using technology to fast-track proven innovations into the healthcare frontline on a Once for Scotland basis. See link:https://www.nhscfsd.co.uk/our-work/innovation/accelerated-national-innovation-adoption-ania-pathway/
