result.text: The ITZBund requires services in the area of software lifecycle management (SLM) for deployed software development and project management solutions. The aim of this tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement to ensure the operation as well as the maintenance and (further) development of the existing software development and project management platform Cloud as well as specialist applications of the ITZBund based thereon. In addition, sovereignty is to be strengthened through the expansion of open source tools to be procured. By open source, the ITZBund understands software whose source code is freely available. In principle, everyone is permitted to use, analyse, modify and pass on this free of charge and without restriction in terms of content regarding object and source code. Specifications of the respective relevant open source licence, in particular regarding licence texts, copyright notices or copyleft effects, remain unaffected. The tendered services comprise services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts, as well as demand-oriented new and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The client, who can call off services commissioned by its customers, is authorised to call off. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place within the ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases allow operation at the client's customers with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the outset are tendered in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services This specification of services considers the subject matter of Lot 4: The subject matter of this lot is the provision of an open source issue tracker including associated training, support, further development and migration services. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract term of 4 years, an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 150.776 staff hours (SH) or 18.847 person days (PD) results for the estimated calculatory costs.

parts.source: Das ITZBund benötigt Dienstleistungen im Bereich des Software Lifecycle Managements (SLM) für eingesetzte Softwareentwicklungs- und Projektmanagementlösungen. Ziel dieser Ausschreibung ist der Abschluss eines Rahmenvertrages zur Sicherstellung des Betriebs sowie der Pflege und (Weiter-)Entwicklung der bestehenden Softwareentwicklungs- und Projektmanagementplattform Cloud sowie darauf aufbauender Fachanwendungen des ITZBund. Zudem soll die Souveränität durch die Erweiterung zu beschaffender Open Source Tools gestärkt werden. Unter Open Source versteht das ITZBund Software, deren Quellcode frei verfügbar ist. Grundsätzlich ist es jedermann gestattet, diese unentgeltlich und inhaltlich unbeschränkt im Objekt- und Quellcode zu benutzen, zu analysieren, zu verändern und weiterzugeben. Vorgaben der jeweils einschlägigen Open Source Lizenz, insbesondere zu Lizenztexten, Urhebervermerken oder Copyleft-Effekten, bleiben unberührt. Die ausgeschriebenen Leistungen umfassen Leistungen entlang des gesamten Software Lifecycle, insbesondere Betriebsleistungen, Pflege- und Supportleistungen, Unterstützungsleistungen im Zusammenhang mit Releases und Rollouts sowie bedarfsorientierte Neu- und Weiterentwicklungen bestehender Software und softwarebezogener Werkzeuge. Abrufberechtigt ist der Auftraggeber, der durch seine Kunden beauftragt Leistungen abrufen kann. rejected.text: Government and the nation face a talent shortfall in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity. The CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service ( CyberAI SFS ) program welcomes proposals that address AI and cybersecurity education and workforce development. CyberAI refers to using AI in cybersecurity as well as providing security and resilience for AI systems. The Scholarship Track provides funding to establish, or to continue, scholarship for service programs with integrated AI and cybersecurity components (CyberAI). Scholarship recipients must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents and work after graduation in the AI or cybersecurity mission of a government organisation for a period of at least the length of the scholarship. The Innovation Track supports projects that enhance preparation of AI and/or cybersecurity professionals. Projects may expand existing educational opportunities, curricula, degree programs, educational pathways, methods and interventions, and partnerships among institutions of higher education, government, and employers. Two statutes authorize this program: 15 USC §7442 (cybersecurity) and 42 USC §18993 (AI). CyberAI SFS aligns with the Executive Order 14277 to prioritize AI within scholarship for service programs. CyberAI is managed by NSF’s Directorate for STEM Education in collaboration with the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

result.text: The contracting authority intends to introduce a company-wide uniform, legally compliant and digital records management system (eFile). The aim of this market exploration is to gain an overview of available solutions as well as established professional, technical and organisational implementation approaches. In particular, insights are to be gained into: - suitable solution architectures and implementation approaches - integration options into the existing system landscape - requirements for operation, support and governance - automation and AI functionalities - licensing, operating and cost models - scalability and future-proofing of the solutions - procedural models for introduction, migration and rollout - experiences from comparable organisations, particularly in the public sector environment and among operators of essential services 1. Initial situation The contracting authority currently has a heterogeneous system and information landscape with different storage locations, applications and documentation forms. Information and documents are stored, among other places, in Microsoft 365 applications (e.g. Outlook, Teams and SharePoint), various document management systems, SAP applications and local storage structures. As an operator of essential services (KRITIS), the contracting authority is subject to special requirements regarding information security, compliance, traceability and the long-term availability of information. The objective is the introduction of a central and standardised digital records management system. 2. Target vision (functional requirements) A solution is sought that in particular supports the following requirements: - Central management and provision of records, documents and information - Role- and permission-based access control - Mapping of file plans, metadata and retention rules - Audit-proof documentation and traceability - Integration of relevant enterprise applications and specialist procedures - Support for automated filing, search and retrieval functions - Scalability for company-wide use The contracting authority is expressly interested in different solution approaches and technological implementation options. 3. Operating and support requirements In addition to the provision of the solution, support services for the operation and further development of the digital records management system are expected. The future solution is to be operated as a cloud-based service (SaaS). The contracting authority shall in particular assume functional control, governance as well as user and role management. The technical operation of the solution is provided by the provider. Support is expected in particular in the following areas: - Maintenance and further development of the solution - Technical support and error analysis - Implementation of updates and release changes - Support for configurations and system adjustments - Support for operation, performance and interface management - Training and qualification offers for administrators and users Solutions are sought with an established cloud operating model, transparent support services and clearly defined service level agreements (SLAs). 4. Questions for the market The contracting authority asks interested companies for feedback on the following points: Solution & architecture - What solution approaches do you offer for the introduction of a digital records management system? - How are file structures, metadata, retention periods and archiving mapped in your solution? - What integration options exist with Microsoft 365, SAP and other enterprise applications? - What automation and AI functions are available? Operation & organisation - How is user, role and permission management carried out? - How are traceability, audit-proofness and auditability ensured? - What governance and compliance functions does your solution offer? - What operating and support models do you offer (e.g. SaaS, on-premises or hybrid)? - What experience do you have regarding the operational effort before and after the introduction of your solution? Scaling & costs - How does your solution scale regarding user numbers, record volumes and organisational units? - What licensing and pricing models are used? - Is the solution multi-tenant capable? - What essential cost and effort factors must be taken into consideration? Introduction & implementation - How is the introduction of your solution typically carried out (e.g. project procedure and phase model)? - What timeframe can empirically be expected for the introduction of a digital records management system? - What success factors and typical challenges should be taken into account on the customer side? - What experience do you have in introducing comparable solutions in public sector companies or at operators of essential services? The contracting authority is initially interested in the submission of company documents, presentations or comparable documents with which the aforementioned questions can be answered. Based on the incoming feedback, the contracting authority reserves the right to conduct in-depth discussions as well as presentation or demonstration appointments with selected companies. In this case, the signing of an NDA is necessary.

parts.source: Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt, eine unternehmensweit einheitliche, rechtskonforme und digitale Aktenführung (eAkte) einzuführen. Ziel dieser Markterkundung ist es, einen Überblick über verfügbare Lösungen sowie etablierte fachliche, technische und organisatorische Umsetzungsansätze zu gewinnen. Insbesondere sollen Erkenntnisse gewonnen werden zu: - geeigneten Lösungsarchitekturen und Umsetzungsansätzen - Integrationsmöglichkeiten in die bestehende Systemlandschaft - Anforderungen an Betrieb, Support und Governance - Automatisierungs- und KI-Funktionalitäten - Lizenz-, Betriebs- und Kostenmodellen - Skalierbarkeit und Zukunftsfähigkeit der Lösungen - Vorgehensmodellen für Einführung, Migration und Rollout - Erfahrungen aus vergleichbaren Organisationen, insbesondere im öffentlichen Umfeld und bei KRITIS-Betreibern 1. Ausgangssituation Der Auftraggeber verfügt derzeit über eine heterogene System- und Informationslandschaft mit unterschiedlichen Ablageorten, Anwendungen und Dokumentationsformen. Informationen und Dokumente werden unter anderem in Microsoft 365-Anwendungen (z. B. Outlook, Teams und SharePoint), unterschiedlichen Dokumentenmanagement-Systemen, SAP-Anwendungen sowie lokalen Ablagestrukturen gespeichert. Als Betreiber Kritischer Infrastrukturen (KRITIS) unterliegt der Auftraggeber besonderen Anforderungen an Informationssicherheit, Compliance, Nachvollziehbarkeit und die langfristige Verfügbarkeit von Informationen. Ziel ist die Einführung einer zentralen und standardisierten digitalen Aktenführung. 2. Zielbild (funktionale Anforderungen) Gesucht wird eine Lösung, die insbesondere folgende Anforderungen unterstützt: - Zentrale Verwaltung und Bereitstellung von Akten, Dokumenten und Informationen - Rollen- und berechtigungsbasierte Zugriffssteuerung - Abbildung von Aktenordnungen, Metadaten und Aufbewahrungsregelungen - Revisionssichere Dokumentation und Nachvollziehbarkeit - Integration relevanter Unternehmensanwendungen und Fachverfahren - Unterstützung automatisierter Ablage-, Such- und Recherchefunktionen - Skalierbarkeit für den unternehmensweiten Einsatz Der Auftraggeber ist ausdrücklich an unterschiedlichen Lösungsansätzen und technologischen Umsetzungsmöglichkeiten interessiert. 3. Betriebs- und Supportanforderungen Neben der Bereitstellung der Lösung werden Unterstützungsleistungen für den Betrieb und die Weiterentwicklung der digitalen Aktenführung erwartet. Die zukünftige Lösung soll als cloudbasierter Dienst (SaaS) betrieben werden. Der Auftraggeber übernimmt insbesondere die fachliche Steuerung, Governance sowie die Benutzer- und Rollenverwaltung. Der technische Betrieb der Lösung wird durch den Anbieter erbracht. Unterstützung wird insbesondere in folgenden Bereichen erwartet: - Wartung und Weiterentwicklung der Lösung - Technischer Support und Fehleranalyse - Durchführung von Updates und Releasewechseln - Unterstützung bei Konfigurationen und Systemanpassungen - Unterstützung bei Betrieb, Performance und Schnittstellenmanagement - Schulungs- und Befähigungsangebote für Administratoren und Anwender Gesucht werden Lösungen mit einem etablierten Cloud-Betriebsmodell, transparenten Supportleistungen sowie klar definierten Service-Level-Vereinbarungen (SLA). 4. Fragestellungen an den Markt Der Auftraggeber bittet interessierte Unternehmen um Rückmeldungen zu folgenden Punkten: Lösung & Architektur - Welche Lösungsansätze bieten Sie für die Einführung einer digitalen Aktenführung an? - Wie werden Aktenstrukturen, Metadaten, Aufbewahrungsfristen und Archivierung in Ihrer Lösung abgebildet? - Welche Integrationsmöglichkeiten bestehen zu Microsoft 365, SAP und weiteren Unternehmensanwendungen? - Welche Automatisierungs- und KI-Funktionen stehen zur Verfügung? Betrieb & Organisation - Wie erfolgt die Benutzer-, Rollen- und Berechtigungsverwaltung? - Wie werden Nachvollziehbarkeit, Revisionssicherheit und Auditierbarkeit sichergestellt? - Welche Governance- und Compliance-Funktionen bietet Ihre Lösung? - Welche Betriebs- und Supportmodelle bieten Sie an (z. B. SaaS, On-Premises oder Hybrid)? - Welche Erfahrungen haben Sie hinsichtlich des Betriebsaufwands vor und nach der Einführung Ihrer Lösung? Skalierung & Kosten - Wie skaliert Ihre Lösung hinsichtlich Nutzerzahlen, Aktenvolumina und Organisationseinheiten? - Welche Lizenz- und Preismodelle kommen zum Einsatz? - Ist die Lösung mandantenfähig? - Welche wesentlichen Kosten- und Aufwandsfaktoren sind zu berücksichtigen? Einführung & Umsetzung - Wie erfolgt typischerweise die Einführung Ihrer Lösung (z. B. Projektvorgehen und Phasenmodell)? - Mit welchem zeitlichen Rahmen ist erfahrungsgemäß für die Einführung einer digitalen Aktenführung zu rechnen? - Welche Erfolgsfaktoren und typischen Herausforderungen sollten auf Kundenseite berücksichtigt werden? - Welche Erfahrungen haben Sie bei der Einführung vergleichbarer Lösungen in Unternehmen des öffentlichen Sektors oder bei Betreibern Kritischer Infrastrukturen? Der Auftraggeber ist zunächst an der Übermittlung von Unternehmensunterlagen, Präsentationen oder vergleichbaren Dokumenten interessiert, mit denen die oben genannten Fragestellungen beantwortet werden. Auf Basis der eingehenden Rückmeldungen behält sich der Auftraggeber vor, mit ausgewählten Unternehmen vertiefende Gespräche sowie Präsentations- bzw. Demonstrationstermine durchzuführen. In diesem Fall ist die Unterzeichnung eines NDAs notwendig.

result.text: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services. The procurement will comprise two Lots: Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue. The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate. The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. Dynamic Market Participation Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register. Supplier registration: CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370) The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline. Lot 1: Core Commercial Data. Lot 1 covers the supply and licensing of core commercial optical EO data for use across the UK public sector. The scope of Lot 1 may include: • Current commercial optical EO data products. • Historic imagery to support temporal analysis, seasonal comparison and change detection. • Associated metadata and quality assurance information. • Licensing rights and permissions required to support public sector access and use. Data delivery, integration support and associated technical services required to support the Authority's intended delivery model. Lot 2: Specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Lot 2 - eligible UK public sector organisations may procure specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities from the awarded supplier via call-off. The scope of Lot 2 may include: • Routine monitoring data services • Higher resolution and tasked data services • Historic and archive data services • Analytics and monitoring services • Validation and decision-support services • Field evidence collection services • Data access, hosting and delivery services associated with specialist EO products and services • Implementation, training and user support services required to support operational use The Lot 2 contract will not create a commitment by the Authority or any User to place a Call-Off Order.

result.text: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety - Development and testing of approaches for the use of digitised regulations and rules in occupational health and safety Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety. Starting point of the project: Digital solutions are useful for the drafting, provision and application of technical rules in the field of occupational health and safety. This applies both to rule-making in the occupational health and safety committees at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (see https://www.bmas.de/DE/Arbeit/Arbeitsschutz/Arbeitsschutzausschuesse/arbeitsschutzausschuesse.html ), as well as to the publication of the rules by the BMAS and their application in companies as well as for advice and enforcement. In the field of standardisation, the concept "Digital Smart Standards" is available from the Digital Standards Initiative by DIN and DKE (IDiS) (see https://www.dke.de/idis ). This was applied as an example in a previous research project F 2542 of the BAuA (see https://www.baua.de/DE/Forschung/Forschungsprojekte/f2542 and project website https://digiasr.blogs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ ). A methodology for the step-by-step development of machine-readable and machine-executable testing rules was derived from this (A. Aziz, D. Napps, M. König, S. Gabriel, A. Richter, S. Voß (2025): Approaches for the transformation of technical rules for workplaces into digital rules. https://www.baua.de/DE/Angebote/Publikationen/Fokus/F2542-2). Subject matter of the contract and objectives: Based on the existing approaches and findings, a study is to be conducted to investigate the extent to which approaches for "Digital Smart Standards" can be transferred to further areas of the body of regulations and rules on occupational health and safety, and whether the occupational health and safety rules drawn up in the occupational health and safety committees can be converted into "Digital Smart Regulations", i.e. into level 2 "Machine-readable document", and further developed in future for level 3 "Machine-readable and executable content" and level 4 "Machine-readable and interpretable content". This study is the subject of the services to be provided by the contractor. The aim is to draw up recommendations for action for the further digitalisation of occupational health and safety regulations and rules in Germany. In key technical application contexts and use cases, which are to be selected in cooperation with the occupational health and safety committees at the BMAS, the processes from creation through management and provision to the operational application of rules as well as implementation options must be considered. Requirements from occupational health and safety regulations and rules must be taken into account in practice, particularly during risk assessments by employers. The contractor must therefore investigate in the project how the contents of the occupational health and safety rules can be applied in exemplary digital implementations of the risk assessment processes and in any existing data models and coordinated with further requirements. The contractor systematically compiles and evaluates the results and derives concrete recommendations for action based on them. The project contributes to making the respective body of rules clearer and easier to apply digitally for users in future, as well as to making the processes for creating, further developing, administering and providing the rules more efficient.

parts.source: Beschaffung forschungsbasierter Leistungen im Projekt "Digital Smart Regulations" für den Arbeitsschutz - Entwicklung und Erprobung von Ansätzen für den Einsatz digitalisierter Vorschriften und Regeln im Arbeitsschutz Lot LOT-0001: Beschaffung von forschungsbasierten Leistungen im Projekt "Digital Smart Regulations" für den Arbeitsschutz. Ausgangspunkt des Vorhabens: Für die Erarbeitung, Bereitstellung und Anwendung Technischer Regeln im Bereich des Arbeitsschutzes sind digitale Lösungen sinnvoll. Das gilt sowohl für die Regelsetzung in den Arbeitsschutzausschüssen beim Bundesministerium für Arbeit und Soziales (siehe https://www.bmas.de/DE/Arbeit/Arbeitsschutz/Arbeitsschutzausschuesse/arbeitsschutzausschuesse.html ), als auch für die Bekanntmachung der Regeln durch das BMAS und deren Anwendung in den Betrieben sowie für Beratung und Vollzug. Im Bereich der Normung liegt von der Initiative Digitale Standards von DIN und DKE (IDiS) das Konzept "Digital Smart Standards" vor (siehe https://www.dke.de/idis ). Dieses wurde in einem vorangegangenen Forschungsprojekt F 2542 der BAuA exemplarisch angewendet (siehe https://www.baua.de/DE/Forschung/Forschungsprojekte/f2542 und Projektwebseite https://digiasr.blogs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ ). Eine Methodik für die schrittweise Erarbeitung von maschinenlesbaren und maschinenausführbaren Prüfregeln wurde daraus abgeleitet (A. Aziz, D. Napps, M. König, S. Gabriel, A. Richter, S. Voß (2025): Ansätze für die Transformation von Technischen Regeln für Arbeitsstätten in digitale Regeln. https://www.baua.de/DE/Angebote/Publikationen/Fokus/F2542-2). Auftragsgegenstand und Ziele: Ausgehend von den vorliegenden Ansätzen und Erkenntnissen ist in einer Studie zu untersuchen, inwieweit Ansätze für "Digital Smart Standards" auf weitere Bereiche des Vorschriften- und Regelwerks zum Arbeitsschutz übertragen werden können und die in den Arbeitsschutzausschüssen erarbeiteten Arbeitsschutzregeln zu "Digital Smart Regulations", also in das Level 2 "Maschinenlesbares Dokument" überführt sowie zukünftig für die Level 3 "Maschinenlesbare und ausführbare Inhalte" und Level 4 "Maschinenlesbare und interpretierbare Inhalte", weiterentwickelt werden können. Diese Studie ist Gegenstand der vom Auftragnehmer zu erbringenden Leistungen. Ziel sind Handlungsempfehlungen für die weitere Digitalisierung von Arbeitsschutzvorschriften und -regeln in Deutschland. In maßgeblichen fachlichen Anwendungskontexten und Anwendungsfällen, die in Zusammenarbeit mit den Arbeitsschutzausschüssen beim BMAS auszuwählen sind, sind die Prozesse von der Erstellung über das Management und die Bereitstellung bis zur betrieblichen Anwendung von Regeln sowie die Umsetzungsmöglichkeiten zu betrachten. Anforderungen aus Arbeitsschutzvorschriften und -regeln sind in der Praxis insbesondere bei der Gefährdungsbeurteilung durch Arbeitgeber zu berücksichtigen. Im Projekt ist daher durch den Auftragnehmer zu untersuchen, wie die Inhalte der Arbeitsschutzregeln in exemplarischen digitalen Umsetzungen der Prozesse der Gefährdungsbeurteilung sowie in ggf. vorhandenen Datenmodellen angewendet und mit weiteren Anforderungen koordiniert werden können. Der Auftragnehmer führt die Ergebnisse systematisch zusammen, wertet sie aus und leitet darauf aufbauend konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen ab. Das Projekt trägt dazu bei, das jeweilige Regelwerk auf Nutzerseite zukünftig übersichtlicher und leichter digital anwendbar zu machen sowie die Prozesse der Erstellung, Weiterentwicklung, Verwaltung und Bereitstellung der Regeln effizienter zu gestalten.

result.text: The subject matter of this procurement comprises the procurement of a SaaS solution, which encompasses various functions and services. The focus is on the provision of an extensive digital communication solution based on OX 8. The MBJS is looking for an experienced contractor capable of providing a corresponding solution based on OX 8 while meeting the specific requirements and needs of a state-level solution for the State of Brandenburg regarding high security standards (BSI IT-Grundschutz), data protection compliance (GDPR), integrity, flexibility and scalability. Lot LOT-0001: Communication solution for 25.000 persons in the education sector (teacher mail). In the year 2019, on behalf of the Ministry for Education, Youth and Sport (hereinafter referred to as MBJS), a complex IT infrastructure was built based on the products Univention UCS and Univention UCS@School, consisting of a central identity management system, hereinafter referred to as IDM, and the groupware and email solution Open Xchange from the manufacturer of the same name, hereinafter referred to as OX. An extensive communication solution was created for 20.000 teaching staff at publicly maintained schools in the State of Brandenburg. The schools mapped in UCS and UCS@School in the form of separate school OUs form the basis for the contexts set up in OX. Each school is thus assigned to a separate context in OX. The creation, modification and deletion of accounts in the IDM are carried out via the specialist procedures developed by the MBJS. After several years of operation, due to the lifecycle of OX, it is necessary to transition to the current version 8. The transition to OX 8 requires extensive changes to the UCS OX connector and the IT infrastructure. The version OX 8 requires Docker runtime environments that are not provided by the existing IT infrastructure. It is not possible to simply update the software in the existing system. The MBJS therefore intends to have the groupware and email solution for teaching staff based on OX operated in future as a SaaS solution by a provider. In this context, the user accounts in the existing IDM shall continue to form the basis for the email mailboxes and the existing provisioning processes shall be retained. Only the mail stack of the existing IT infrastructure is to be replaced by a SaaS solution.

parts.source: Der Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung umfasst die Beschaffung einer SaaS-Lösung, welche verschiedene Funktionen und Leistungen umfasst. Dabei liegt der Schwerpunkt auf der Bereitstellung einer umfangreichen digitalen Kommunikationslösung auf Basis von OX 8. Das MBJS sucht nach einem erfahrenen Auftragnehmer, der in der Lage ist, eine entsprechende Lösung auf Basis von OX 8 bereitzustellen und dabei die spezifischen Anforderungen und Bedürfnisse einer Landeslösung für das Land Brandenburg in punkto hohe Sicherheitsstandards (BSI Grundschutz), Datenschutzkonformität (DSGVO), Integrität, Flexibilität und Skalierbarkeit zu erfüllen. Lot LOT-0001: Kommunikationslösung für 25.000 Personen im Bildungsbereich (Lehrermail). Im Jahr 2019 wurde im Auftrag des Ministeriums für Bildung, Jugend und Sport (im Folgenden MBJS genannt) auf Basis der Produkte Univention UCS und Univention UCS@School eine komplexe IT-Infrastruktur aufgebaut, bestehend aus einem zentralen Identitätsmanagement-System, im Folgenden als IDM bezeichnet, und der Groupware- und E-Mail-Lösung Open Xchange vom gleichnamigen Hersteller, im Folgenden als OX bezeichnet. Es wurde eine umfangreiche Kommunikationslösung für 20.000 Lehrkräfte an Schulen in öffentlicher Trägerschaft im Land Brandenburg geschaffen. Die in UCS und UCS@School abgebildeten Schulen in Form von separaten Schul-OUs bilden die Grundlage für die in OX eingerichteten Contexte. Jede Schule ist somit einem separatem Context in OX zugewiesen. Das Anlegen, Ändern und Löschen von Accounts im IDM, erfolgt über die vom MBJS entwickelten Fachverfahren. Nach mehreren Jahren des Betriebs, ist es aufgrund des Lifecycles von OX erforderlich, dass auf die aktuelle Version 8 gewechselt werden muss. Mit dem Wechsel auf OX 8 bedarf es einer umfangreichen Änderungen am UCS OX Connector und an der IT-Infrastruktur. Die Version OX 8 setzt Docker-Laufzeitumgebungen voraus, die mit der bestehenden IT-Infrastruktur nicht gegeben sind. Es ist nicht möglich die Software im bestehenden System einfach zu aktualisieren. Das MBJS beabsichtigt deshalb die Groupware- und E-Mail-Lösung für Lehrkräfte auf Basis von OX zukünftig als SaaS-Lösung durch einen Anbieter betreiben zulassen. Dabei sollen die Nutzerkonten im vorhandenen IDM weiterhin die Grundlage für die E-Mail-Postfächer bilden und die bestehenden Prozesse zur Provisionierung beibehalten werden. Es soll lediglich der Mail-Stack der vorhandenen IT-Infrastruktur durch eine SaaS-Lösung ersetzt werden.

result.text: The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) established a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) to procure Work Focused Activities for Jobcentre Plus Districts in England, Scotland and Wales via the previous DWP eProcurement Solution (ePS). DWP has now migrated to a new ePS, Atamis and DWP are therefore reissuing this notice via the Atamis portal. However, please note that 'online' applications to join the FSF DPS 2 via the Atamis Portal are currently suspended and a temporary 'offline' process is in place, further details are below. The DPS is for the procurement of social and other services referred to in Regulation 74 of the Public Contracts Regulations (2015) and as such, the intention is to use a light touch regime, rather than the full regime described in Regulation 34 (Dynamic Purchasing System). The DPS is for the sole use of DWP. The Flexible Support Fund Dynamic Purchasing System 2 - For the Provision of Work Focused Activities (FSF DPS 2) is the replacement for the DWP Dynamic Purchasing System for provision of work-focused activities known as the Flexible Support Fund DPS (FSF DPS). The FSF DPS expired on 31 October 2021 and was replaced by the FSF DPS 2 with effect from 1 November 2021. Currently the 'online' application process is suspended, and a temporary 'offline' process is in operation. Any new supplier wishing to apply to join the FSF DPS 2 should send an email to cdfsf.adhocprocurement@dwp.gov.uk requesting to apply to join the FSF DPS 2, and the relevant information will be sent to you via email. Although DWP are currently operating an 'offline' process to join the FSF DPS 2, suppliers will still be required to create an account on Atamis. Suppliers can do this via the link below, which will take you to the DWP Atamis landing page. To ensure that the page functions correctly, you must accept browser cookies https://dwp2.my.site.com/s/Welcome From this landing page, new suppliers will be able to create an Atamis account by selecting the "Supplier Registration Here" button and following the on screen instructions. The landing page also has a link to the Supplier Portal Help page, where you will find an article to help with registering for an account https://suppliersupport.atamis.co.uk/hc/en-gb/articles/4613254620319-Registering-with-a-Supplier-Portal Estimated overall value of this DPS will be £250,000,000.00 Additional Information As of 1 January 2021, the internationally comparable regional geography for the UK is the International Territorial Levels (ITLs) geography. This has replaced the Nomenclature of territorial units for statistics (NUTS) geographies for the UK that were operational when the UK was a member of the European Union. Please refer to the spreadsheet to see how the NUTS Code correspond to the ITL Codes at Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3.

result.text: Crown Estate Scotland (CES) is seeking a contractor to lead the survey and reporting of our tenant groups on the Scottish Crown Estate. CES has been surveying its tenants since 2017, with survey providing important feedback on CES performance, the service we provide and the relationship we have with our tenants Lot 1: . Crown Estate Scotland (CES) is seeking a contractor to lead the survey and reporting of our tenant groups on the Scottish Crown Estate. CES has been surveying its tenants since 2017, with survey providing important feedback on CES performance, the service we provide and the relationship we have with our tenants. There has been a break in survey while we have been developing our new corporate plan, with the last surveys carried out in 2023. This contract will align with our new corporate plan timeframe 2026-2031 with two surveys required – one in the first year of the Corporate Plan, scheduled for August this year (2026). And a second survey in year four of the corporate plan in FY 2029/30. Surveys are of our three main tenant groups – Property, Energy and Infrastructure, and Aquaculture, with reporting against a number of sub-groups under these. Previously different tenant groups were surveyed separately, with a rolling programme of surveys across a three-year cycle. For this contract we will survey all tenant groups together, requiring only one survey and reporting cycle in 2026 and again in 2029/30. Key to this survey will be reporting against the new corporate plan KPI on customer satisfaction ‘Customer satisfaction is increased by 10% over the plan period from the 2026 baseline’. Some support will be required on survey development and framing. All previous tenant surveys have been led by a contractor, adding transparency, objectivity and impartiality to the survey, helping to engender tenant trust and confidence in the process. Please note that the first survey must be completed in August 2026.

And a second survey in year four of the corporate plan in FY 2029/30. Surveys are of our three main tenant groups – Property, Energy and Infrastructure, and Aquaculture, with reporting against a number of sub-groups under these. Previously different tenant groups were surveyed separately, with a rolling programme of surveys across a three-year cycle. For this contract we will survey all tenant groups together, requiring only one survey and reporting cycle in 2026 and again in 2029/30. Key to this survey will be reporting against the new corporate plan KPI on customer satisfaction ‘Customer satisfaction is increased by 10% over the plan period from the 2026 baseline’. Some support will be required on survey development and framing. All previous tenant surveys have been led by a contractor, adding transparency, objectivity and impartiality to the survey, helping to engender tenant trust and confidence in the process. Please note that the first survey must be completed in August 2026.

result.text: ESPO is a public sector-owned professional buying organisation offering a comprehensive range of procurement services, including access to over 100 free-to-access framework solutions for the wider public sector. We are establishing a framework to cover the provision document management solutions including digitisation, off-site storage, and confidential shredding of documents. The Framework is divided into 7 lots. Please refer to the tender documents for any further details (including further details on each of the lots) - the closing date for submission of Tenders is 12:00 (12 noon / 12pm) on 12 October 2026. To tender (please proceed to step (e) if an expression of interest has already been completed): (a) Go to https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ (b) Register (if not already registered on ProContract e.g., via https://procontract.due-north.com/Register); (c) Search for tender opportunity 390_27 (via "View Opportunities" from the EastMidsTenders Portal, or alternatively via searching on https://procontract.due-north.com/Opportunities/Index); (d) Express an interest; (e) Download the tender documents (from the ProContract Activity summary screen). Any questions or clarifications relating to this tender opportunity should be submitted to ESPO as a message on the eProcurement Portal, once an Expression of interest has been completed. Lot 1: Electronic Document Scanning and Software. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to-end scanning solution including preparation, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents. To include the supply, implementation and maintenance of EDRM (Electronic Document & Records Management Software), associated Project management and training. Lot 2: Document Storage and Retrieval Services. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide preparation, collection, storage, retrieval and the secure disposal of documents plus any associated services. Lot 3: Total Document Management Solution. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to end solution for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated training. Suppliers will also be required to provide a consultancy Service designed to scope and shape a full document management solution to help customers manage all their documents. Lot 4: Enhanced Handling and Security Requirements. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide enhanced safe and secure document management solutions for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes secure handling of documents, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated and training. Lot 5: Confidential On-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide on-site confidential shredding services. Lot 6: Confidential Off-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide off-site confidential shredding services. Lot 7: On-Site and Off-Site High Security Shredding to NPSA Standards. This Lot requires suppliers to provide high security shredding services to NPSA standards.

result.text: Pohjois-Karjalan hyvinvointialue (Siun sote) is renewing its medical device register to meet current requirements for data management, usability, traceability and integration. The system must be a ready-for-use, operational SaaS-based medical device register system that supports the management of devices used in social and health care operations. Medical devices and instruments can be stored in the register. The solution must support the lifecycle management of the devices, ensure the up-to-dateness and integrity of data, and enable role-based use by different user groups for desktop, browser and mobile use. The procurement includes the system licence, implementation and delivery project including integrations, data migration from the current system, maintenance and support services and normal system version updates, as well as other services defined in the tender documents. The more detailed content of the delivery and the requirements concerning it are described in the tender documents and their appendices. During the preparation phase of the procurement, the contracting authority has conducted a market dialogue by publishing a request for information on Hilma 17.2.2026, announcement name Tietopyyntö: Lääkintälaiterekisteri, Hilma number 2026-041337, announcement reference/diary number 598561. By means of the market dialogue, the contracting authority has surveyed solutions available on the market and evaluated alternatives suitable for the contracting authority's needs. The information obtained in the market dialogue has been taken into account in the preparation of the procurement, but the requirements of the invitation to tender have been defined on the basis of the contracting authority's own actual needs.

parts.source: Pohjois-Karjalan hyvinvointialue (Siun sote) uudistaa lääkintälaiterekisterinsä vastaamaan nykyisiä tiedonhallinnan, käytettävyyden, jäljitettävyyden ja integraatioiden vaatimuksia. result.text: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET CONSULTATION AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: This information request is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority will not initiate a tendering procedure by publishing the information request, but a potential contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The responses given to this information request will be used in planning the procurement of overall services related to the maintenance and operation of HUS's internal network, the "HUSnet network". HUS-yhtymä's IT Management is planning to renew the comprehensive service agreement for the HUSnet network. The computer network is a critical part of HUS-yhtymä's operations and includes a wide infrastructure of approx. 250 sites in the Uusimaa region as well as connections to cloud services. The equipment base consists of, among other things: - approx. 3 000 L2/L3 switches - approx. 10 000 WLAN access points - firewall environments - peripheral systems. The purpose of the information request and market dialogue is to survey various solution alternatives with which HUS-yhtymä's network environment can be maintained and developed, taking into account potential future requirements. Market dialogues will be held during February-March as in-person or Teams meetings. Service providers are requested to register by 11.2.2026 at kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Subject of the message: "HUS 580-2025/HUSnet services". In their responses, service providers are hoped to present their key service descriptions related to, among other things, network management, maintenance and development. In addition, presentations of reference implementations are desired. Advance material speeds up the dialogue held in the meeting. When proceeding to the procurement phase, suppliers who have responded to the information request may receive preliminary tender documents for comment.

rejected.text: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales. These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: - An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. - A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense. - An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System - A Warehouse Management System - Other BI Reporting Systems The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment. The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement. The main objectives of this exercise are to: - Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS), - Test market capability and capacity, - Validate the proposed scope and service model, - Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and - Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project. Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk). When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that: - the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions; - they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the of the service; and - they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments. Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October. There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered. Lot 1: . None

result.text: Description of the Project: Local Governance Reform Programme (LGRP) III The "Multi-Donor Action (EU-BMZ) - Strengthening Capacities and Institutional Readiness of Reform Actors in Palestine" co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, aims to enhance the institutional capacity, operational effectiveness, and coordination functions of MoFP and PMO ERO as leading entities in national planning and reform management. The Action will support MoFP in its role as the central coordinating body for national planning by enhancing its capacity to embed data-driven policymaking, ensure coherent approaches across line ministries, and improve coordination across all levels of governance. The Palestinian Authority (PA) faces significant institutional and technical challenges in managing, measuring, and demonstrating public sector performance. Monitoring and evaluation (M&E) functions across line ministries and agencies (LMAs) are narrowly defined, fragmented, and largely disconnected from planning and budgeting decisions. Indicators are poorly formulated, feeder data is weak and uncoordinated, and M&E reporting serves administrative compliance rather than evidence-based management. The Strategic Results Framework (SRF), which is the principal instrument for measuring national results delivery, lacks a usable structure, theory of change, and coherent indicator set. No overarching national M&E strategy exists, and data management responsibilities across government institutions remain undefined and unanchored. Lot LOT-0001: 10037895-Development of a National M&E System in Palestine. Description of Work and Services to be Provided: structured around eight work packages (WPs) covering the full cycle from system design through operationalization, capacity development, and digital enablement. WP1: Inception, Alignment, and Mobilization. It establishes the analytical and operational foundation for the assignment. The contractor reviews and consolidates the OECD/Sigma diagnostic findings, conducts targeted design assessments to collect operational information required for subsequent WPs, including data feasibility mapping, institutional baseline mapping, planning-budgeting process validation, pilot site readiness assessment, and a digital systems inventory. The contractor establishes the governance and coordination arrangements, detailed workplan, stakeholder engagement plan, and risk register. The primary deliverable is a comprehensive Inception Report. WP2: National M&E System Framework and Governance. It produces the foundational design of the national M&E system, developed jointly with MoFP and key government stakeholders rather than as an externally designed product. It defines the system"s purpose, scope, institutional roles, governance mechanisms, core M&E processes, data governance principles, integration logic with planning and budgeting, evaluation framework, and system stewardship mandate. The deliverable is a government-endorsed National M&E Framework. WP3: Results and Measurement Architecture. It redesigns the Strategic Results Framework using a methodology-first, pilot-based approach that accounts for the current limitations of the national development plan. The contractor develops a comprehensive SRF methodology and standards framework designed for the next national planning cycle, conducts a participatory results clarification exercise with a pilot of sectors, and produces a transitional indicator set for the remaining current planning cycle to enable piloting. Deliverables include the revised SRF Methodology Document and the Updated SRF and Indicator Framework. WP4: Institutional and Functional Design. It defines the organizational arrangements required to anchor M&E and data management as permanent government functions. Through a participatory process with MoFP and LMAs, the contractor develops functional design models, organizational options with feasibility assessments against General Personnel Council (GCP) civil service frameworks, RACI matrices, workflow systems, and HR alignment proposals. The deliverable is an Institutional and Functional Design Report. WP5: Integration with Planning, Budgeting, and Oversight. It defines how M&E information can flow into and influences core government decision-making processes, including annual planning, budget preparation, and performance oversight at CoM level. The contractor maps actual planning and budgeting processes, assesses linkage feasibility, designs standard decision-informing M&E products, and proposes integration mechanisms. Deliverables include M&E Integration Framework and Updated Planning and Budgeting Guidance Notes. WP6: Operationalization and Piloting. It translates the system design into operational reality through co-developed SOPs, data collection instruments, reporting templates, and interim digital tools, tested with 3-5 pilot LMAs selected on the basis of a readiness assessment conducted in WP1. The pilot tests real workflows and data flows, generating feedback that is incorporated into system refinements. The deliverable is a Pilot Implementation Report. WP7: Capacity Development, Change Management, and Sustainability. It builds the professional and institutional capacities required for sustained system operation. The contractor develops competency frameworks, training programs, and materials; delivers training in two waves; designs and initiates change management and communication strategies; proposes institutionalization and incentive mechanisms in coordination with GPC; and, importantly, builds system stewardship capacity enabling MoFP and LMAs to maintain, update, and evolve the system independently after assignment conclusion.

result.text: The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/ Unlike many space faring nations in the Charter, the UK Government does not own or operate its own national EO satellite system assets. The UK Government therefore fulfils its Charter commitments through partnership with the UK EO commercial sector. This procurement seeks to maintain and strengthen that model by securing operational support from an organisation with UK licensed and operated EO satellite data assets that can be contributed to Charter activations. The continued participation of UK EO commercial satellite operators in the Charter delivers both public benefit and strategic value by showcasing sovereign EO capabilities, supporting international disaster response and demonstrating operational utility of UK-developed EO missions. The Contracting Authority is intending to launch this requirement by the 9th of October - prospective bidders should note it may launch earlier at the Contracting Authority's discretion: all dates provided are estimates at this stage. Lot 1: . None

The local authority has therefore applied for and received approval for funding for area-wide gigabit expansion - relating to the underserved sub-area in the economic viability gap model within the framework of the directive "Funding to support the gigabit expansion of telecommunications networks in the Federal Republic of Germany - Federal Gigabit Directive 2.0 (Gigabit-RL 2.0)" of 31. March 2023 in the version of the 1. Amendment of 30.04.2024 ("Gigabit Directive 2.0"). The funding provided in this funding programme in the economic viability gap model (hereinafter: funds) is to be passed on by local authorities to telecommunications companies within the meaning of EU state aid law as investment cost subsidies for the construction and operation of gigabit networks.

result.text: IKOMM AS invites tenderers, on behalf of Enebakk municipality, to a market survey for the procurement of a new map and management system for water and sewage. Enebakk municipality shall procure a new map and management system for water and sewage in autumn 2026 in the municipality. The municipality needs a future orientated, comprehensive and user-friendly system for managing the water and sewage network. The system shall support both administrative and operative activities and facilitate efficient interaction between employees in offices and personnel in the field. The system must be available via modern web technology and function on different devices (PCs, tablets and mobile), so that registration, updating and posting can be carried out where the work actually takes place. The system shall support efficient registration and management of the pipeline network, manholes and the accompanying technical installations, including the use of GNSS/GPS equipment for precise surveying. The system shall meet strict requirements for information security and stand-by, reduce operational and maintenance costs and ensure that the municipality meets the current environmental and reporting requirements. >: We would like to carry out a market survey (RFI) in order to gain insight into relevant systems, technology and suppliers. Furthermore, we would like to invite up to 3 tenderers to public dialogue meetings to take a closer look at the options that can offer to ensure a good future orientated procurement. Other municipalities in the region will also be invited to participate in this market survey in order to possibly participate in a future competition. > > > > The dialogue meetings are planned to be held in early April as physical meetings in IKOMM ́s premises in Vinterbro, but with an option for participation in Teams. Relevant tenderers will be selected based on relevance, experience and references from equivalent and comparable municipal systems. The objective of the market survey is to: * Gain insight into what systems and suppliers are available in the market * Examine how the tenderers handle technical requirements, integration, security and stand-by * Using the knowledge to improve the requirement specifications and choice of procurement strategy. > This market dialogue will be carried out as a voluntary and non-binding request for information (Request for Information – RFI), cf. FOA § 9-3 and § 12-2, which allow contracting authorities to obtain information about the market before any competition. > > This is not part of a competition and does not involve any obligations for Enebakk municipality or for the tenderers who choose to provide answers. > > Tenderers who participate in the market dialogue will not be given any kind of competition, and participation (or lack of participation) will not lead to exclusion from a later competition. Any future procurements will be implemented in accordance with public procurement regulations, and all tenderers will be able to compete on equal terms. > We therefore invite interested suppliers to provide written input and possibly participate in dialogue meetings. Participation is voluntary and the market dialogue is not binding for the municipality or suppliers. Good if suppliers can give feedback on the possibility of participation in the dialogue meetings that are planned. > attached a disposition/questionnaire for the market survey. > All dialogue will take place in the KDV tool Artifik for traceability. Please use Artifik support if this tool is unknown to suppliers.

rejected.text: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications to develop, operate, and sustain a cloud-based data storage and computing platform that democratises access to large-scale Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) genetic and genomic data. The platform must be secure, scalable, and interoperable. The platform will support the NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), the primary NIA-supported repository for the archiving and distribution of human genetic data related to AD/ADRD. The purpose of the platform will be to: Enable efficient ingestion, curation, harmonisation, and analysis of multi-ancestry, large population-scale datasets; Provide robust analysis, visualisation, and artificial intelligence -ready resources within secure cloud workspaces; Ensure compliance with federal security and data-sharing policies; Promote interoperability with other NIH- and NIA-supported repositories; and Provide user support, training, and community engagement. The NOFO aims to foster collaboration, accelerate discovery, and maximise the scientific value and impact of AD/ADRD genetics research for the broader research community. By improving data accessibility, interoperability, reporting, reproducibility, and scalable computational systems that enable rigorous, reproducible, and transparent research, the NOFO seeks to align with the NIH’s plan for Gold Standard Science and the AD/ADRD Research Implementation Milestones . Additionally, the NOFO seeks to address the Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's recommendation of ensuring broad, secure access to high-value datasets and enhancing data usability to maximise the return on research investments and support future discoveries in AD/ADRD. Moreover, the NOFO intends to directly advance NIA’s Strategic Directions , particularly Goal G to support the infrastructure and resources necessary for high-quality research, by strengthening data sharing, computational infrastructure, and research rigour across the AD/ADRD community. The NOFO intends to utilise the U24 activity code. Applications are not being solicited at this time. This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.

result.text: The KVB intends to replace its existing SAP HCM landscape, which is also used for the group company KSG, by way of a carve-out and to transform it to SAP SuccessFactors as a full cloud solution. The contract covers the preparation, implementation, and operational phases, in particular conception and preparation of the requirements specification, implementation, configuration and customising, data migration, integration and interface adaptation, testing, training, project management, change management support, go-live and hypercare, as well as subsequent support during productive operation. In particular, Employee Central, Employee Central Payroll, Time Tracking, Learning, Onboarding, and WalkMe Premium for SuccessFactors are to be introduced. SAP S/4HANA, SAP Integration Suite, and SAP BW on HANA are to be included in particular. The required SuccessFactors licences are already available and are not the subject of the contract. In addition, an optional quota of up to 1.000 person-days is provided for supplementary services. Full productive operation is scheduled for no later than 01.06.2028. Details regarding the scope of services and binding requirements can be found in the service description and the other tender documents. The following binding minimum requirements or knock-out criteria apply to the tender phase: 1. The personnel deployed for the provision of services must possess sound to long-standing, extensive, and in-depth experience and knowledge regarding SAP HCM and SuccessFactors. The bidder must guarantee this in its tender. 2. The bidder must guarantee that the provision of services complies with the current state of the art and recognised technical rules as well as the principle of sensible, appropriate, and economical use, also with regard to further costs such as, in particular, operating costs. In justified cases of doubt, compliance with these requirements must be proven at the contractor's expense. 3. The project language is German. All documentation, minutes, reports, planning, and training materials must be written entirely in German. Meetings, workshops, and training sessions must be conducted in German. The specialist personnel deployed must have a fluent command of the German language in both speech and writing. If German is not the native language, at least a German language diploma of level C1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required. 4. All of the bidder's employees, including external subcontractors and freelancers, must comply with the provisions of the General Data Protection Regulation. The bidder may only deploy persons for whom a written declaration of consent to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation is available. 5. The offered solution must in particular meet the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation, the Federal Data Protection Act, the principles for the proper keeping and storage of books, records, and documents in electronic form, and for data access, as well as other statutory retention and documentation obligations. 6. Completed personnel-related processes, data sets, documents, and records may only be deleted or archived after the expiry of the respective applicable statutory or professional retention periods. The corresponding process must be designed in a legally compliant and audit-proof manner and documented by means of procedural documentation. Failure to meet any of these minimum requirements will lead to the exclusion of the tender. The individual and sub-criteria, their weighting, the evaluation method including the linking of price and performance, the scoring scale, any minimum scores, as well as the information and evidence to be submitted will be provided uniformly to the selected applicants with the invitation to submit the indicative initial tender. They will specify the aforementioned award framework.

parts.source: Die KVB beabsichtigt, ihre bestehende, auch für die Konzerngesellschaft KSG genutzte SAP-HCM-Landschaft im Wege eines Carve-outs abzulösen und auf SAP SuccessFactors als Full-Cloud-Lösung zu transformieren. Der Auftrag umfasst die Vorbereitungs-, Umsetzungs- und Betriebsphase, insbesondere Konzeption und Pflichtenhefterstellung, Implementierung, Konfiguration und Customizing, Datenmigration, Integration und Schnittstellenanpassung, Test, Schulung, Projektmanagement, Unterstützung des Change Managements, Go-live und Hypercare sowie die anschließende Unterstützung im Produktivbetrieb. Einzuführen sind insbesondere Employee Central, Employee Central Payroll, Time Tracking, Learning, Onboarding und WalkMe Premium for SuccessFactors. Einzubeziehen sind insbesondere SAP S/4HANA, SAP Integration Suite und SAP BW on HANA. Die erforderlichen SuccessFactors-Lizenzen sind bereits vorhanden und nicht Gegenstand des Auftrags. Ergänzend ist ein optionales Kontingent von bis zu 1.000 Personentagen für ergänzende Dienstleistungen vorgesehen. Der vollständige Produktivbetrieb ist spätestens zum 01.06.2028 vorgesehen. Die Einzelheiten zum Leistungsumfang und zu den verbindlichen Anforderungen ergeben sich aus der Leistungsbeschreibung und den weiteren Vergabeunterlagen. Für die Angebotsphase gelten folgende verbindliche Mindestanforderungen beziehungsweise K.-o.-Kriterien: 1. Das für die Leistungserbringung eingesetzte Personal muss über fundierte bis langjährige, umfangreiche und tiefgehende Erfahrungen und Kenntnisse in Bezug auf SAP HCM und SuccessFactors verfügen. Der Bieter muss dies in seinem Angebot zusichern. 2. Der Bieter muss zusichern, dass die Leistungserbringung dem aktuellen Stand und den anerkannten Regeln der Technik sowie dem Grundsatz einer sinnvollen, zweckmäßigen und wirtschaftlichen Nutzung, auch hinsichtlich weiterer Kosten wie insbesondere der Betriebskosten, entspricht. Im begründeten Zweifelsfall ist die Einhaltung dieser Vorgaben auf Kosten des Auftragnehmers nachzuweisen. 3. Die Projektsprache ist Deutsch. Sämtliche Dokumentationen, Protokolle, Berichte, Planungs- und Schulungsunterlagen müssen vollständig in deutscher Sprache verfasst werden. Besprechungen, Workshops und Schulungen sind in deutscher Sprache durchzuführen. Das eingesetzte Fachpersonal muss die deutsche Sprache fließend in Wort und Schrift beherrschen. Sofern Deutsch nicht die Muttersprache ist, wird mindestens ein deutsches Sprachdiplom der Stufe C1 nach dem Gemeinsamen Europäischen Referenzrahmen verlangt. 4. Sämtliche Mitarbeiter des Bieters einschließlich externer Unterauftragnehmer und freier Mitarbeiter müssen die Bestimmungen der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung einhalten. Der Bieter darf nur Personen einsetzen, für die eine schriftliche Einverständniserklärung zur Einhaltung der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung vorliegt. 5. Die angebotene Lösung muss insbesondere die Anforderungen der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung, des Bundesdatenschutzgesetzes, der Grundsätze zur ordnungsmäßigen Führung und Aufbewahrung von Büchern, Aufzeichnungen und Unterlagen in elektronischer Form sowie zum Datenzugriff und der weiteren gesetzlichen Aufbewahrungs- und Nachweispflichten erfüllen. 6. Abgeschlossene personalbezogene Vorgänge, Datenbestände, Dokumente und Nachweise dürfen erst nach Ablauf der jeweils geltenden gesetzlichen oder fachlichen Aufbewahrungsfristen gelöscht oder archiviert werden. Der entsprechende Prozess muss gesetzeskonform und revisionssicher ausgestaltet sowie durch eine Verfahrensdokumentation dokumentiert werden. Die Nichterfüllung einer dieser Mindestanforderungen führt zum Ausschluss des Angebots. Die Einzel- und Unterkriterien, deren Gewichtung, die Bewertungsmethode einschließlich der Verknüpfung von Preis und Leistung, die Punkteskala, etwaige Mindestpunktzahlen sowie die einzureichenden Angaben und Nachweise werden den ausgewählten Bewerbern einheitlich mit der Aufforderung zur Abgabe des indikativen Erstangebots zur Verfügung gestellt. Sie konkretisieren den vorstehenden Zuschlagsrahmen.

result.text: The object of the procurement is the testing equipment for the ETCS subsystems of the Digirail testing laboratory, the related software, and the installation, maintenance, development, support and training services related to the entity. The main objective of the Digirail testing laboratory is to ensure that the systems procured in the Digirail project meet all technical and operational requirements, support the integration and interoperability of the ETCS system, and are ready for the SIT and SAT testing phases. The details of the request for participate and the request for tender can be found in the appendix documents in Finnish and English.

result.text: Background Registers of Scotland (RoS) is undertaking a strategic review of its current data licensing position as part of its ambition to maximise the value of the data it holds. RoS currently delivers a range of statutory and commercial data products to a diverse customer base, including citizens, public sector bodies, and commercial organisations. This breadth of demand has led to an increasing need to develop scalable and sustainable data products. The development of these products is shaped by existing licensing arrangements, including the Public Sector Geospatial Agreement (PSGA) and Postal Address File (PAF) frameworks. These define the terms under which data can be used, reused, and shared, particularly where third-party data is integrated with RoS datasets. RoS is seeking specialist support to work with existing RoS departments to define a data strategy that reflects the organisation’s current and future priorities. Purpose of this Notice This notice is issued to engage with the market and identify organisations with expertise in public sector data licensing, data commercialisation, and governance. The feedback received will inform the scope, structure, and requirements of a potential future procurement exercise. Scope of Potential Requirement RoS is seeking a partner to provide expertise and support in the following areas covering both current and future activity. 1. Review of Current Licensing Landscape Assess RoS’s current licensing arrangements, including PSGA, PAF, and other third party agreements Identify constraints, risks, and opportunities in the current model Advise on how existing frameworks can be leveraged to support data products and services while ensure statutory obligations remain paramount 2. Definition of Data Principles Support RoS in developing clear data principles covering: Data sharing and reuse Commercialisation and monetisation Transparency, fairness, and public value Ensure alignment with public sector obligations, corporate objectives and customer expectations 3. Recommendations and Implementation Roadmap Provide actionable, practical recommendations for: Optimising the use of RoS data Enabling new data products and services Managing licensing risks and compliance Clear options, trade-offs, and decision frameworks to support senior decision-making Develop an implementation roadmap that RoS can deliver internally 4. Capability and Skills Development Identify the organisational skills, roles, and capabilities required to: Sustain data commercialisation Govern data and licensing frameworks effectively Recommend approaches to embed these capabilities within RoS operations Key Context for Suppliers RoS operates within a complex licensing environment, particularly where third party data is embedded in its products There is a tension between legacy licensing models and ambitions for more open, scalable data products, which has been identified as a systemic issue RoS is exploring different strategic options, including changes to licensing arrangements and potential use of external partners to support commercialisation Market Engagement RoS invites expressions of interest from organisations with experience in: Public sector data licensing and governance Data commercialisation and product development Navigating complex multi party licensing frameworks Supporting organisations to unlock the value of their data assets Responses to this notice will help shape the design of any future procurement.
